title: Bifrost Configuration Schema
description: Schema for Bifrost HTTP transport configuration

$schema.description: Schema location for IDE validation. Defaults to "https://www.getbifrost.ai/schema" and can be set to a mirrored URL, file:// URL, or filesystem path for isolated deployments.

read_buffer_size.description: Read buffer size in bytes. This controls the size of the buffer used for reading HTTP headers.

body_buffer_pool_limit_bytes.description: Largest request-body buffer (in bytes) a pooled keep-alive connection keeps for reuse between requests. Larger buffers are released after each request so connections do not pin their largest-ever body in memory; larger bodies are still accepted up to the max request body size. Not set uses the default (4 MiB); 0 means unlimited and keeps every buffer. Process-wide: also applies to outbound fasthttp request buffers. Deploy-time only.

plugin_download_private_allowlist.description: Hostnames, IP addresses, or CIDR ranges that custom plugin (.so) downloads are allowed to reach even when they resolve to a private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT address (blocked by default to prevent SSRF). Use only for trusted internal artifact hosts. Deploy-time only - read from config.json/environment at startup, never settable via the plugin admin API.

a2a_grpc_base_domain.description: Base domain for the Agent Gateway's shared gRPC listener. Served agent cards advertise per-agent hostnames (<agent-name>.<base-domain>:<port>); a wildcard DNS record for *.<base-domain> must point at this server, and requests are routed by the first DNS label of the dialed authority. Deploy-time only; gRPC stays disabled while this or a2a_grpc_port is unset.

a2a_grpc_port.description: Advertised (public) port for the Agent Gateway's shared gRPC listener. When a load balancer or port mapping sits in front, the BIFROST_A2A_GRPC_LISTEN_PORT environment variable overrides the local bind port without changing what agent cards advertise. Deploy-time only; gRPC stays disabled while this or a2a_grpc_base_domain is unset.

a2a_allow_private_push_callbacks.description: Allows Agent push delivery to loopback and private network destinations. Intended only for controlled development and test environments. Disabled by default; all other outbound SSRF protections are unchanged.

version.description: Controls how empty arrays in the allow-list fields of provider keys (models) and virtual keys (allowed_models, key_ids, tools_to_execute) are interpreted. Omit or set to 2 for v1.5.0+ semantics: empty = deny all, ["*"] = allow all. Set to 1 to restore v1.4.x semantics: empty = allow all. Projects under governance.projects are not affected: their allow-lists always treat empty or omitted as granting nothing, whatever this is set to.

source_of_truth.description: Controls how config.json is reconciled with the config store. "split" preserves existing merge behavior. "config.json" makes present config.json sections authoritative during startup sync; missing sections leave database rows untouched.

encryption_key.description: You can set the value as env.<ENV_VAR_NAME> to use an environment variable. We also read encryption key from BIFROST_ENCRYPTION_KEY environment variable. Note: once set, the encryption key cannot be changed unless you clean up the database. Accepts any string; a secure 32-byte AES-256 key will be derived using Argon2id KDF. If not provided, data will be saved in plain text. Recommended: use a passphrase of at least 16 bytes for better security

env_label.description: Short label (max 10 characters) displayed in the management UI sidebar to identify the environment (e.g. "staging", "prod"). Overrides the BIFROST_ENV_LABEL environment variable when both are set.

disable_onboarding.description: Hides the management UI setup checklist for every user. Unlike the in-app "hide for everyone" action, this is read from config.json on every start and never written to the config store, so it stays in effect on stateless deployments (ephemeral container storage, provider-less log viewers). Overrides the BIFROST_DISABLE_ONBOARDING environment variable when both are set.

setup_token.description: Operator-provisioned bootstrap secret required to create the very first admin account when no admin account is configured yet. In OSS, while dashboard auth is not active (no admin account, or auth disabled), every /api call must carry this value in the X-Bifrost-Setup-Token header. You can set the value as env.<ENV_VAR_NAME> to use an environment variable, or as vault.<path> to use a Vault secret reference. We also read the setup token from the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable. Identical across every node in a multi-node deployment (unlike a randomly generated value), so any node can authorize first-admin creation. Never persisted and never logged; if left unset, creating the first admin account is rejected until this is configured. Whitespace-only values are rejected.

drop_excess_requests.description: Whether to drop excess requests when pool is full

initial_pool_size.description: Initial size of the connection pool

prometheus_labels.description: Labels to use for Prometheus metrics

allowed_origins.description: CORS allowed origins: exact URI strings, wildcard-host patterns such as https://*.example.com, or "*". While dashboard auth is disabled, browser requests to the management API are accepted only from localhost origins, the gateway's own origin, and origins listed here explicitly; the "*" entry does not admit them.

disable_content_logging.description: Disable logging of sensitive content (inputs, outputs, embeddings, etc.)

retain_content_in_object_storage.description: When content logging is disabled, offload the full content to object storage as hidden instead of dropping it. Hidden content is never served back through the API/UI — the database row stays metadata-only and is only readable with direct access to the storage bucket. Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store.

allow_per_request_content_storage_overri.description: Allow individual requests to override content storage via the x-bf-disable-content-logging header or context key, and to opt in to raw-byte persistence in logs via x-bf-store-raw-request-response. When false (default), the global disable_content_logging setting is authoritative and per-request storage overrides are ignored. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers — see allow_per_request_raw_override.

allow_per_request_raw_override.description: Allow individual requests to send raw provider request/response bytes back to the caller via the x-bf-send-back-raw-request and x-bf-send-back-raw-response headers. When false (default), the provider-level send_back_raw_request/response settings are authoritative and per-request overrides are ignored. Does not affect raw-byte persistence in logs — see allow_per_request_content_storage_override.

disable_db_pings_in_health.description: Disable DB pings in health check

dump_errors_in_console_logs.description: Dump full error details to the server console logs. Useful for debugging; may be noisy in production.

webhook_config.description: Global webhook delivery settings; per-endpoint tuning lives on each endpoint. Read at server startup.

delivery_history_retention_days.description: How long delivery history records are kept before being reaped.

log_retention_days.description: Number of days to retain logs

enforce_auth_on_inference.description: Require auth (VK, API key, or user token) on inference endpoints. Defaults to true on new deployments and when creating the first enabled admin account if omitted; explicit false opts out. Existing deployments retain their stored setting when omitted.

dual_credential_conflict_behavior.description: Controls behavior when an inference request carries both an IDP access token (Authorization: Bearer <jwt>) and a virtual key (x-bf-vk header). 'error' rejects with 400. 'prefer_vk' drops the IDP token and authenticates via the VK. 'prefer_idp' (default) uses the IDP token for identity.

extra_fields_placement.description: Where inference responses carry Bifrost's extra_fields metadata. 'body' (default) keeps the extra_fields object in the JSON body. 'headers' removes extra_fields from the body (and from every streaming chunk) and sends its scalar fields as x-bifrost-* response headers. In 'headers' mode the large and nested fields are dropped and not sent anywhere: raw_request, raw_response, routing_metadata, guardrail_debug, parse_errors, and on errors key_statuses, billed_usage and mcp_auth_required. Streaming responses only carry the fields known before the first chunk (routing identity, fallback index, cache lookup); per-chunk latency, chunk_index and final totals are dropped.

max_request_body_size_mb.description: Maximum request body size in MB. Also the ceiling for what a compressed request body may decompress to: within it a body may expand to at most 100 times its compressed size (1 MiB floor), and at most four times this cap of decompressed request bytes are held in flight at once

compat.description: Compat plugin configuration for request type conversion, parameter dropping, and parameter value conversion

convert_text_to_chat.description: Convert text completion requests to chat for models that only support chat

convert_chat_to_responses.description: Convert chat completion requests to responses for models that only support responses

should_drop_params.description: Drop unsupported parameters based on model catalog allowlist

should_convert_params.description: Converts model parameter values that are not supported by the model.

azure_deepseek.description: Convert Azure DeepSeek responses requests to chat completions so reasoning is preserved for coding harnesses.

force_reasoning_only_models_to_responses.description: Convert chat completion requests to responses for models whose datasheet sets supports_reasoning_with_tool_calls to false, so reasoning is kept instead of being forced off.

convert_decision_to_responses.description: Emulate decision requests through the model's Responses API (a forced function tool) when the provider does not serve the model on a native decisions endpoint. Off by default: without it, such requests fail with unsupported_operation.

header_filter_config.description: Global header filtering configuration for x-bf-eh-* headers forwarded to LLM providers

allowlist.description: If non-empty, only these headers (from x-bf-eh-* prefix) are allowed to be forwarded

denylist.description: Headers to always block from being forwarded

async_job_result_ttl.description: Default TTL for async job results in seconds (default: 3600 = 1 hour)

required_headers.description: Headers that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of these headers are rejected with 400. Case-insensitive matching.

logging_headers.description: Headers to capture in log metadata. Values are extracted from incoming requests and stored in the metadata field of log entries.

whitelisted_routes.description: Routes that bypass auth middleware. Requests to these exact paths skip authentication checks.

hide_deleted_virtual_keys_in_filters.description: When true, deleted virtual keys are omitted from logs and MCP logs filter data.

hidden_request_types.description: Request types excluded from dashboard and log API reads. Logs are still stored; an empty array shows all request types. Editable from the UI under Logs Settings.

allowed_headers.description: Additional allowed headers for CORS and WebSocket

allow_direct_keys.description: Allow callers to bypass the registered key pool by supplying x-bf-direct-key: true and the provider's raw API key in an Authorization (Bearer), x-api-key, or x-goog-api-key header.

delete_expired_virtual_keys.description: Delete expired virtual keys automatically. A daily cleanup job removes every key whose expiry has passed unless the key sets delete_after_expire to false; keys with delete_after_expire true are removed regardless.

enforce_vk_object_ownership.description: Restrict provider objects (files, batches, videos, containers, container files, cached contents and live sessions) to the virtual key that created them. Another virtual key gets 404 for them and does not see them in list responses. Requests without a virtual key are not restricted. Creators are recorded even while this is off, so turning it back on also covers objects created meanwhile; an object whose creator could not be recorded stays reachable to every virtual key.

skip_access_profile_user_virtual_key_cre.description: Enterprise only. When true, a user's first access profile never creates a virtual key for them. Keys the user already owns are still governed by the profile while they hold one.

skip_access_profile_user_virtual_key_del.description: Enterprise only. When true, removing a user's last access profile never deletes their virtual keys; they are kept as ordinary keys with none of the profile's providers or access. Deleting the user still deletes their keys.

vk_rotation_cooldown.description: Cooldown after virtual key rotation: grace period during which the previous key value still authenticates. Accepts a Go duration string (e.g. "5m", "1h"); integer values are nanoseconds (Go duration JSON encoding), so prefer strings. 0 or an empty string disables the grace period (the old value stops working immediately). Maximum 30 days (2592000000000000 ns); string durations are bounds-checked at runtime.

mcp_agent_depth.description: DEPRECATED: Maximum depth for MCP agent mode tool execution. Use mcp.tool_manager_config.max_agent_depth.

mcp_tool_execution_timeout.description: DEPRECATED: Timeout for individual MCP tool execution in seconds. Use mcp.tool_manager_config.tool_execution_timeout.

mcp_code_mode_binding_level.description: DEPRECATED: Code mode binding level for MCP tools. Use mcp.tool_manager_config.code_mode_binding_level.

mcp_tool_sync_interval.description: DEPRECATED: Global tool sync interval in minutes (0 = default of 10 minutes). Use mcp.tool_sync_interval.

mcp_disable_auto_tool_inject.description: DEPRECATED: When true, MCP tools are not automatically injected into requests. Use mcp.tool_manager_config.disable_auto_tool_inject.

mcp_code_mode_limits.description: Per-execution code mode limits, as stored and served by the config API. In config.json prefer mcp.tool_manager_config.code_mode_limits, which takes precedence when both are set.

mcp_oauth_private_allowlist.description: Hostnames, IP addresses, or CIDR ranges (no schemes or ports) that the MCP OAuth chain (discovery, dynamic client registration, token requests) may reach even when they resolve to a loopback or private address. Applies only to MCP clients registered by an authenticated admin or declared in config.json; clients registered while dashboard auth was off stay public-only. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are always refused and cannot be listed. As stored and served by the config API; changing it over the API requires an authenticated admin session. In config.json prefer mcp.tool_manager_config.oauth_private_allowlist, which takes precedence when both are set.

mcp_enable_temp_token_auth.description: When true, Bifrost mints and accepts scoped temp tokens for MCP per-user OAuth and per-user-headers auth pages so anonymous browser visitors can complete the flow without a dashboard session. User-mode flows are never minted regardless of this setting — they always require SSO login.

routing_chain_max_depth.description: Maximum depth for routing rule chain evaluation

mcp_external_client_url.description: Public base URL Bifrost uses as the redirect_uri when acting as an OAuth client to upstream MCP servers (Notion, Jira, etc.). Set when Bifrost's callback endpoint is reached via a different URL than its server-side metadata. Supports env var syntax: "env.MY_VAR".

skills_external_client_url.description: Public base URL for Skills Repository marketplaces. Required to enable Claude Code and Codex marketplace serving; skill management and downloads remain available when unset. Supports env var and vault references.

a2a_store_raw_request_response.description: Capture upstream A2A transport bodies before SDK conversion. HTTP bodies preserve JSON-RPC envelopes and SSE framing. Raw capture is unavailable for gRPC. Stored as base64, bounded to 1 MiB per direction, and subject to the shared content logging policy.

a2a_private_allowlist.description: Private hosts, IP addresses, or CIDR ranges Agent Gateway discovery, OAuth, and runtime requests may reach. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are always blocked.

a2a_external_client_url.description: Bifrost's public base URL for the Agent Gateway, used in served agent cards and push-notification callback URLs. Required to enable Agent Gateway protocol endpoints. When unset, agent traffic is rejected while management APIs remain available. Supports env var syntax: "env.MY_VAR".

mcp_server_auth_mode.description: How /mcp authenticates inbound MCP clients. 'headers' (default): VK/api-key/session headers only, discovery disabled. 'both': accepts header credentials and Bifrost-issued JWTs, discovery enabled. 'oauth': Bifrost JWTs only — WARNING: disables VK/header MCP access.

allowed_redirect_uris.description: Exact remote OAuth client callback URIs approved by the administrator. Local loopback and cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp callbacks are permitted without entries. Remote callbacks are denied by default; a bare "*" entry allows any https callback; private-use scheme callbacks still need an exact entry, and partial wildcards are rejected. Changing this list through the API requires dashboard authentication.

issuer_url.description: Stable public URL advertised as the OAuth2 AS issuer in discovery documents and JWT iss claim. Required whenever mcp_server_auth_mode is 'both' or 'oauth' (config load and PUT /api/config reject an unset value in those modes); the issuer is never derived from the request Host header while OAuth is enabled. Supports env var syntax: "env.MY_VAR".

auth_code_ttl.description: Lifetime of the single-use authorization code in seconds (default: 300, max: 900 = 15 minutes).

access_token_ttl.description: Lifetime of the issued JWT Bearer token in seconds (default: 600).

disable_vk_identity.description: When true, the OAuth consent flow no longer offers or accepts virtual-key identity and existing virtual-key grants lose access immediately (rejected at request time and unable to refresh). Honored only when an identity provider is configured. Only valid when mcp_server_auth_mode is 'oauth'.

oauth2_server_config.description: OAuth2 authorization server settings for /mcp. Only relevant when mcp_server_auth_mode is 'both' or 'oauth'.

governance.description: Governance configuration for budgets, rate limits, customers, teams, virtual keys, and routing rules

reset_config.description: Window settings the reset duration cannot express. Only valid when reset_duration is quarterly ('1Q').

quarter_start_month.description: First month of Q1 as 1-12, so a fiscal year opening in April (4) gives Apr-Jun / Jul-Sep / Oct-Dec / Jan-Mar. Omitted or 0 means January. Quarter boundaries repeat every three months, so only the value modulo 3 changes the reset dates: January, April, July and October all reset on calendar quarters and differ only in which quarter is labelled Q1.

current_usage.description: Seed value only: current usage in dollars, applied when the budget is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter - the value here is ignored on every subsequent sync so a config.json reload cannot overwrite live accounting.

last_reset.description: Seed value only: last time the budget was reset, applied when the budget is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter, like current_usage.

virtual_key_id.description: ID of the virtual key this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with provider_config_id)

provider_config_id.description: ID of the provider config this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with virtual_key_id)

model_config_id.description: ID of the model config this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with the other owner IDs)

customer_id.description: ID of the customer this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with the other owner IDs)

team_id.description: ID of the team this budget belongs to (mutually exclusive with virtual_key_id and provider_config_id)

calendar_aligned.description: Deprecated: set calendar_aligned on the owner (team / virtual key / access profile) instead. Kept for backward compatibility with older config.json files; ignored unless a reconciler promotes it to its owner.

override_amount.description: Amount added to max_limit while an override is active

override_mode.description: How long the override stays active: 'cycles' for a finite number of reset windows, 'forever' until explicitly removed, '' for no override

override_cycles_remaining.description: Reset windows the current override still covers, including the current one. Derived state: recomputed from override_anchor_reset, override_cycles_total and last_reset, so it is never the source of truth.

override_cycles_total.description: Number of reset windows the current finite override was granted for. Immutable for the life of a grant.

override_anchor_reset.description: Window boundary at which the current finite override was granted. Immutable for the life of a grant; absent when there is no finite override.

token_current_usage.description: Seed value only: current token usage, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter - the value here is ignored on every subsequent sync so a config.json reload cannot overwrite live counters.

token_last_reset.description: Seed value only: last time the token counter was reset, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter, like token_current_usage.

request_current_usage.description: Seed value only: current request usage, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter - the value here is ignored on every subsequent sync so a config.json reload cannot overwrite live counters.

request_last_reset.description: Seed value only: last time the request counter was reset, applied when the rate limit is first created. Runtime-owned thereafter, like request_current_usage.

calendar_aligned.description: Deprecated: set calendar_aligned on the owner (team / virtual key / access profile) instead. Kept for backward compatibility with older config.json files; ignored unless a reconciler promotes it to its owner.

budgets.description: Inline budget configurations for this customer. Each entry must have a unique reset_duration. Mutually exclusive with budget_id.

budget_id.description: Single budget reference (pre-declared in governance.budgets). Deprecated in favour of inline budgets.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) this customer holds. The profile governs everything under the customer and replaces its own budgets and rate limit, so it cannot be combined with them. Under source_of_truth "split" the declaration is applied when it is new or changed and dashboard changes are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is enforced on every startup and an entry without access_profile has its profile removed.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap the customer's budget and rate-limit reset windows to clean calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year)

virtual_key_count.description: Computed count of virtual keys associated with this customer

source_id.description: Optional external source identifier (e.g. SCIM group ID) used to map this team to an upstream system. Unique when set.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) this team holds. The profile governs everything under the team and replaces its own budgets and rate limit, so it cannot be combined with them. Under source_of_truth "split" the declaration is applied when it is new or changed and dashboard changes are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is enforced on every startup and an entry without access_profile has its profile removed.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap the team's budget and rate-limit reset windows to clean calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year)

virtual_key_count.description: Computed count of virtual keys associated with this team

business_units.description: Business unit configurations with optional team assignments

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) this business unit holds. The profile governs everything under the business unit and replaces its own budgets and rate limit, so it cannot be combined with them. Under source_of_truth "split" the declaration is applied when it is new or changed and dashboard changes are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is enforced on every startup and an entry without access_profile has its profile removed.

team_ids.description: Team IDs to assign to this business unit

roles.description: RBAC role definitions. Roles are created or updated on startup if the config hash changes; system roles and dashboard-created roles are never deleted.

dac.description: Data Access Control scope: own-data (user's own records), team-data (plus records of the user's teams), business-unit-data (plus records of the user's business units), customer-data (everything under the customers the user reaches through their teams or business units), all-data (unrestricted). Defaults to all-data.

entity_dac.description: Per-entity Data Access Control overrides, keyed by resource name. Each entry narrows or widens the role's global dac for that one entity; entities not listed follow dac. Resources accepting an override as of this release: Logs, MCPLogs, AuditLogs, VirtualKeys, Users, Teams, Customers, BusinessUnits, RBAC, APIKeys, AccessProfiles, PromptRepository, RoutingRules, GuardrailsConfig, MCPGateway, VirtualMCPs, Projects.

access_profile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) to attach as the default for this role. Changing this field triggers a re-sync on next startup. Leave unset to let the dashboard manage the assignment.

access_profiles.description: Names of all access profiles granted by this role. When present, this field takes precedence over access_profile; an empty list removes all profile grants.

permissions.description: List of resource+operation permission pairs to grant to this role

resource.description: Permission resource (e.g. Logs, VirtualKeys, Users, ModelProvider, Metrics, Guardrails, AccessProfiles, MCPToolGroups, Roles, BusinessUnits, AuditLogs, Billing)

operation.description: Permission operation (e.g. View, Create, Update, Delete, Download, RunInference, ManageInference, ViewInference)

projects.description: Projects: per-request access gates and accounting scopes that requests opt into. Matched by name and created or updated on startup when the config hash changes; membership is managed from the dashboard and is never declared here.

value.description: The virtual key value. A literal, or an "env.VAR"/"vault.path" reference resolved to plaintext at load time.

is_active.description: Whether the virtual key is active

expires_at.description: Optional expiry timestamp (RFC3339). Once passed, requests using this virtual key are rejected. Omit for a key that never expires.

delete_after_expire.description: Delete this virtual key automatically once expires_at has passed. A daily cleanup job removes it and posts a notification. Omit to follow client.delete_expired_virtual_keys; true or false override it for this key. Requires expires_at.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap all budget resets to calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year)

allow_all_providers.description: Grant this virtual key access to every provider, including ones added later. Coexists with provider_configs: a provider that also has a config row still has that config's model allow/blacklist, budgets, rate limits, and key selection applied; providers without a config get all models, all keys, and no per-provider limits. When false (default), access is deny-by-default via provider_configs.

disable_content_logging.description: Per-key override of client.disable_content_logging for requests made with this virtual key. Omit to inherit the client setting. true keeps request and response content out of the log store and out of OpenTelemetry export for this key's traffic; other observability connectors follow their own disable_content_logging until they adopt the trace mark. When content logging ends up disabled for a request, the log row is still written without content; with client.retain_content_in_object_storage on and an object-storage-backed log store, the full payload is then kept there as hidden content that the API and UI never serve. false forces content into the log store even when the client setting is true; observability connectors keep following their own disable_content_logging. The x-bf-disable-content-logging request header, when client.allow_per_request_content_storage_override is on, still takes precedence over this value for the log store.

metadata.description: Custom key/value metadata for this virtual key (for example cost_center, project, owner, environment). Copied onto every log entry the key produces, so logs and spend can be filtered by it; on a key collision it overrides request-supplied log metadata (x-bf-lh-* headers, configured logging headers, x-bf-dim-* dimensions). Keys may contain letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' (max 256 characters) and may not be system-reserved (isAsyncRequest, bifrost_alb_*); values are strings of at most 512 characters; at most 50 entries.

team_id.description: Associated team ID (mutually exclusive with customer_id and business_unit_id)

customer_id.description: Associated customer ID (mutually exclusive with team_id and business_unit_id)

business_unit_id.description: Associated business unit ID (mutually exclusive with team_id and customer_id)

access_profile_id.description: Deprecated and ignored: direct access-profile assignment was reverted in v1.5.9 (#3669/#3670) and the column dropped. Accepted only for backward-compatible validation of older config files.

is_access_profile_managed.description: Read-only, server-computed flag: true when the virtual key is governed by an access profile. Never persisted and ignored if set in config.json.

assigned_user.description: Read-only, server-populated projection of the user this virtual key is assigned to. Present as an object (or null when resolved but unassigned) on governance read paths; omitted when the assignee could not be resolved. Never persisted and ignored if set in config.json.

provider_configs.description: Provider configurations for this virtual key (empty means no providers allowed, deny-by-default)

mcp_configs.description: MCP configurations for this virtual key (empty array means no MCP tools allowed, deny-by-default)

agent_grants.description: Agent grants directly assigned to this virtual key (empty array means no agents allowed, deny-by-default)

relay_grants.description: Relays this virtual key may call, one by one (empty means no relays allowed, deny-by-default)

allOf.$comment: A virtual key belongs to at most one owner: team_id and customer_id cannot both name one.
A virtual key belongs to at most one owner: team_id and business_unit_id cannot both name one.
A virtual key belongs to at most one owner: customer_id and business_unit_id cannot both name one.

routing_rules.description: Routing rules for dynamic provider/model selection based on CEL expressions

pricing_overrides.description: Scoped pricing overrides applied at runtime by the model catalog

model_configs.description: Per-model rate limit and budget configurations

model_name.description: Model name to apply the configuration to

provider.description: Optional provider name to scope this config

scope.description: Scope where this config applies: "global" (default) or "virtual_key"

scope_id.description: Target entity ID for non-global scopes (e.g. virtual key ID). Required when scope != "global"

calendar_aligned.description: Snap this config's budget resets to calendar boundaries (e.g. a monthly budget resets on the 1st) rather than rolling windows. For virtual_key-scoped configs it inherits the virtual key's setting.

budget_id.description: Deprecated — single budget reference. Use budget_ids instead.

budget_ids.description: List of budget IDs (from governance.budgets) to associate with this model config. Supports multiple budgets (e.g. daily + monthly). Replaces budget_id.

rate_limit_id.description: Rate limit ID to associate with this model

store_raw_request_response.description: Capture raw request/response for internal logging only; strip from API responses returned to clients (default: false)

ignore_provider_cost.description: Ignore the provider-reported usage.cost and calculate cost from Bifrost's model pricing and pricing overrides (default: false)

alerting.description: Enterprise alerting configuration for governance-backed alert channels, rules, history retention, and outbound webhook URL validation.

history_retention_days.description: Number of days to retain alert history. Omit to use the default. Set to 0 to disable retention pruning.

webhook_network.description: Outbound URL validation controls for Slack, Microsoft Teams, and generic webhook alert channels.

allow_http.description: Allow alert webhooks to use http URLs. By default only https URLs are accepted.

allow_private_network.description: Allow alert webhooks to target private or loopback network addresses. Useful for local testing.

channels.description: Declarative alert channels synced into the enterprise config store at startup.

enabled.description: Whether this alert channel can receive notifications.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between sends for this channel. Set to 0 for no channel-level cooldown.

url.description: Generic webhook URL. Supports env.VAR_NAME references.

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the webhook request. Values support env.VAR_NAME references. Sensitive hop-by-hop headers are ignored at send time.

rules.description: Declarative alert rules synced into the enterprise config store at startup.

scope_id.description: ID of the virtual key, team, or customer referenced by scope_type.

cel_expression.description: CEL expression evaluated against alerting usage variables such as budget_usage_percent, budget_spent, request_usage, token_usage, and rate-limit percentages.

channel_ids.description: IDs of alert channels to notify when this rule matches.

target_type.description: Optional explicit target type. Use budget with target_id to evaluate one specific budget; omit to evaluate all budgets for the scope.

webhooks.description: Webhook endpoint declarations synced into the database at startup, reconciled by name.

id.description: Stable endpoint ID. Generated when omitted.

url.description: Delivery URL. HTTPS required unless allow_private_network is set; credentials and fragments are rejected; link-local and metadata addresses are always blocked.

secret.description: Signing secret in the whsec_ format. Best supplied as an env reference ("env.MY_VAR"); generated when omitted.

include_response.description: Inline the job response into delivery payloads, capped by max_response_payload_kbs.

disabled.description: Register the endpoint without delivering to it.

retry_backoff_initial_seconds.description: Delay before the first retry in seconds; each further retry doubles it (default: 30).

retry_backoff_max_seconds.description: Cap on the per-retry delay in seconds (default: 1800).

attempt_timeout_seconds.description: End-to-end bound for one delivery attempt in seconds (default: 10).

max_response_payload_kbs.description: Cap for inlined response/error payloads in KB when include_response is set (default: 256). Oversized values are omitted and flagged with response_omitted/error_omitted.

max_concurrent_deliveries.description: Concurrent in-flight deliveries to this endpoint per node (default: 10).

agents.description: Declarative A2A agent registrations reconciled into the config store at startup. name.description: Unique registration name (URL-safe slug). Forms the gateway routes /agents/a2a/<name>/... and the gRPC hostname label.

agent_card_url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the upstream agent's Agent Card (typically .../.well-known/agent-card.json).

allow_by_default.description: Allow access for any identified caller without an explicit virtual-key grant (default: false).

forward_accepted_credential.description: Forward the accepted Bifrost credential to the upstream agent so its callback LLM/MCP requests route back through Bifrost (default: false).

forward_accepted_credential_overrides_au.description: When forwarding the accepted credential, replace the configured runtime auth Authorization header with it instead of sending it alongside (default: false).

discovery_auth.description: Authentication used when fetching the upstream Agent Card.

runtime_auth.description: Authentication attached to proxied upstream agent requests.

credential_origins.description: Additional HTTP(S) origins permitted to receive runtime credentials and client certificates. Include scheme and optional port, without paths, queries, fragments, or userinfo. The agent card origin is permitted automatically.

virtual_key_ids.description: Virtual key IDs granted access to this agent. Declares the exact grant set: changes here are reconciled like any other field.

relays.description: Relays reconciled into the config store at startup, before governance so virtual keys can grant them. Matching is by name with hash-based change detection; in config.json source-of-truth mode stored endpoints absent from this list are pruned.

max_protocol_version.description: Newest MCP protocol version Bifrost offers to upstream MCP servers. 'auto' uses the newest version Bifrost supports. tool_sync_interval.description: Global default interval for syncing tools from MCP servers (Go duration string in whole minutes, e.g. '10m', '1h', '1h30m'; '0s' uses the runtime default of 10 minutes). Legacy integer nanoseconds are also accepted and must be a whole number of minutes.

virtual_mcps.description: Virtual MCPs: named bundles of tools from one or more MCP clients, served at /mcp/<endpoint_slug> and attachable to virtual keys. Canonical key; supersedes the deprecated tool_groups alias.

tool_groups.description: DEPRECATED: use virtual_mcps instead. Enterprise MCP tool groups with optional governance associations. Kept for backward compatibility.

enabled.description: Enable configuration store

args.description: Arguments passed directly to the executable

cache_ttl.description: How long a resolved password is reused across new physical connections (Go duration string, default 60s). Without caching the command runs on every new connection. Keep this below the credential's validity window: a rotation shorter than the TTL will fail connections until the cached value expires.

max_idle_conns.description: Maximum number of idle connections in the pool (default: 5)

max_open_conns.description: Maximum number of open connections to the database (default: 50)

conn_max_lifetime.description: Maximum lifetime for physical database connections as a Go duration string

conn_max_idle_time.description: How long an idle physical connection is kept before being closed (Go duration string, default 5m). Without this the idle cap alone controls pool size, so bursts above max_idle_conns close and reopen connections repeatedly. Note the logs store and config store open separate pools, so a pod's connection ceiling is the sum of their max_open_conns.

statement_timeout.description: Server-side statement_timeout set on every runtime pool connection (Go duration string, default 120s). Bounds a runaway query so it cannot hold a pooled connection and its locks indefinitely. "0" or a negative value leaves the server default. Migrations and background index builds are never bound by it.

idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.description: Server-side idle_in_transaction_session_timeout set on every runtime pool connection (Go duration string, default 120s). Ends a session left idle inside an open transaction, which would otherwise hold row locks and block vacuum. "0" or a negative value leaves the server default.

migration_lock_retry_budget.description: How long a schema migration step keeps retrying after lock timeouts before the process gives up and exits (Go duration string, default 10m). During a rolling upgrade a step that needs a table lock retries while older replicas' long queries hold the table; raise this on large deployments so the budget outlasts those queries, and keep the Kubernetes startup probe at least as long. Each lock timeout logs the sessions holding the table so an operator can cancel them instead of waiting.

prefix.description: Path prefix applied to every secret (default: bifrost)

access_mode.description: read_only resolves existing refs only; read_and_write also auto-stores plaintext fields and deletes owned secrets. Defaults to read_only.

azure.description: Azure Key Vault configuration. Set client_id and client_secret (with tenant_id) to use a service principal; omit them to use DefaultAzureCredential (workload identity, managed identity, or AZURE_* environment variables).

matview_refresh_interval.description: How often to refresh dashboard materialized views. Go duration string (e.g. '1m', '5m', '1h'). Default 1m. Raise this when matview refresh CPU cost is material on the database instance. Positive values below 5s are clamped up to 5s. Set 'off' or a zero duration (e.g. '0s') to disable materialized-view maintenance entirely; dashboard queries fall back to the raw tables.

matview_refresh_timeout.description: Maximum time for a single materialized view refresh pass. Go duration string, min 30s, max 30m. Unset derives a budget from matview_refresh_interval (5x the interval, at least 5m). A refresh holds a pooled connection and a session advisory lock across every view, so without a bound one stuck refresh leaves the views permanently stale across all replicas.

matview_refresh_temp_file_limit.description: Caps the temp files each Postgres process running a materialized view statement may write (Postgres temp_file_limit, e.g. '10GB'; parallel workers each get the cap). A refresh over a very large logs table can spill tens of GB, and a full disk fails every query on the server. A statement that hits the cap fails and the view keeps its previous contents. Unset leaves the server setting alone. The database role needs superuser or GRANT SET ON PARAMETER temp_file_limit; without it the cap is skipped with a warning.

migration_matview_cancel_after.description: How long schema migrations wait for an in-flight materialized view refresh pass (from any replica, including older releases during a rolling upgrade) before cancelling its REFRESH statements. Migrations pause refreshes for their whole run, because a long refresh on a large logs table blocks their CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and ALTER TABLE logs statements. A cancelled concurrent refresh rolls back and the view keeps its previous contents. Go duration string; unset uses 60s; "off" never cancels and only waits.

port.description: ClickHouse port. Defaults by protocol: native 9000 (9440 TLS), http 8123 (8443 TLS)

secure.description: Enable TLS (native: secure=true; http: switches to https)

max_query_size.description: ClickHouse max_query_size setting in bytes, the longest SQL text the server will parse (default: 16777216)

cluster.description: Optional cluster name; when set, DDL runs ON CLUSTER with replicated table engines

writer.description: Async logging writer queue and batch tuning. Omitted fields use runtime defaults.

max_batch_bytes.description: Approximate byte-size ceiling for a batch before flushing (default: 314572800)

write_queue_capacity.description: Buffered queue capacity for pending log writes (default: 10000). This queue is also the buffer while the writer pauses for another node's log store migration, so it bounds how much of that window is absorbed without drops.

deferred_usage_concurrency.description: Maximum concurrent deferred usage database updates (default: 5)

object_storage.description: Optional object storage for offloading LLM and MCP log payloads. When configured, full payloads are stored in S3/GCS/Azure Blob while the DB keeps lightweight index data. MCP log rows keep dashboard/table fields plus a 200-character input preview.

bucket.description: Bucket name, or Azure Blob container name. Supports env var reference (e.g. env.S3_BUCKET) or a structured secret reference.

prefix.description: Key prefix for stored objects (default: bifrost)

compress.description: Legacy gzip switch, equivalent to compression "gzip". An explicit compression value takes precedence. Default: false

format.description: Encoding of offloaded log payload objects. json writes {id}.json.gz objects; parquet writes single-row {id}.parquet files (one UTF8 column per payload field) readable by Athena, Spark and DuckDB. Objects written before a format change stay readable. parquet is supported on s3 and azure. Default: json

compression.description: Compression for offloaded log payload objects. For json it is applied to the whole object (none or gzip only). For parquet it is the page codec inside the file (none, gzip, snappy or zstd), and no outer gzip is added. Default: none for json (gzip when compress is true), snappy for parquet.

region.description: AWS region. Supports env var reference

endpoint.description: Custom S3-compatible endpoint for MinIO/R2. Supports env var reference

access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID. Omit to use default credential chain (instance role, env vars, etc.). Supports env var reference

secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key. Supports env var reference

session_token.description: AWS session token for STS temporary credentials. Supports env var reference

role_arn.description: AWS IAM role ARN for STS AssumeRole. Works with static creds or instance role. Supports env var reference

force_path_style.description: Use path-style URLs for S3 (required for MinIO). Default: false

credentials_json.description: GCP service account credentials JSON or file path. Omit to use Application Default Credentials. Supports env var reference

credentials.description: Deprecated: use credentials_json. Kept for backwards compatibility.

project_id.description: GCP project ID override. Supports env var reference

format.description: parquet is not supported for gcs yet

object_storage_exclude_request_types.description: Request types (log object type, e.g. list_models, embedding) whose logs are not offloaded to object storage. These logs are written to the logs database in full instead. Hidden logs (content logging disabled with client.retain_content_in_object_storage on) are still offloaded, so their content never lands in the database.

object_storage_exclude_fields.description: LLM log payload field DB column names that should NOT be offloaded to object storage and must remain in the database (e.g. output_message, input_history, raw_request, raw_response). Unknown names are ignored. error_details always remains in the database (except on content-hidden logs), since the error type, error code and status code breakdowns query it; any raw provider bodies inside it are offloaded unless error_details is listed here. MCP logs always offload the full log and keep dashboard/table fields plus a 200-character input preview in the database.

retention_days.description: Days to retain log entries. 0 disables retention-based cleanup.

skills_registry.description: Declarative Skills Repository definitions reconciled from config.json

skills.description: Skills to create or update from config.json

path.description: Path to the plugin (optional, required for dynamic plugins)

placement.description: DB-Backed Only. Whether this plugin runs before, after, or as a built-in. Default: post_builtin. Setting or changing it here reloads the plugin entry from config.json; omit it and the stored value is kept.

order.description: DB-Backed Only. Position within placement group. Lower values execute earlier. Default: 0. Setting or changing it here reloads the plugin entry from config.json; omit it and the stored value is kept.

semaphore_size.description: For plugins that implement ObservabilityPlugin (receive completed traces): cap on how many traces may be injected into this plugin concurrently. A saturated cap causes new traces to be dropped for this plugin only, not process-wide. Ignored by plugins that don't receive traces (default: 10000).

inject_timeout.description: For plugins that implement ObservabilityPlugin: timeout for a single Inject call from the tracer, as a Go duration string (default: 5s). Bounds how long a hung connector can hold a concurrency-budget slot. Ignored by plugins that don't receive traces.

config.description: Configuration for the telemetry plugin (Prometheus metrics)

custom_labels.description: Custom labels to add to Prometheus metrics

metrics_enabled.description: Serve the /metrics scrape endpoint. Defaults to true when omitted.

overhead_breakdown_enabled.description: Export the per-component overhead histogram bifrost_overhead_component_microseconds (overhead latency split by the overhead_component label). Off by default. Requires tracing to be active, since the breakdown is computed from completed trace spans.

user_labels_enabled.description: Add user_id and user_name labels to every bifrost_* metric. Off by default: these are unbounded, so they multiply metric series by end-user count on top of a virtual_key_id label that already reaches tens of thousands of values in large deployments. Prometheus holds every label combination in memory for the retention period and cannot drop a label afterwards. Per-user attribution is available without this from BigQuery columns or Splunk event fields.

push_gateway.description: Configuration for pushing metrics to a Prometheus Push Gateway for multi-node cluster deployments

enabled.description: Whether to enable pushing metrics to the Push Gateway

push_gateway_url.description: URL of the Prometheus Push Gateway (e.g., http://pushgateway:9091)

instance_id.description: Instance identifier for grouping metrics. If not set, hostname is used automatically.

basic_auth.description: Basic authentication credentials for the Push Gateway

disable_content_logging.description: Disable logging of request and response content

retain_content_in_object_storage.description: When content logging is disabled, offload the full content to object storage as hidden instead of dropping it. Hidden content is never served back through the API/UI. Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store.

allow_per_request_content_storage_overri.description: Allow individual requests to override content storage via the x-bf-disable-content-logging header or context key, and to opt in to raw-byte persistence in logs via x-bf-store-raw-request-response. When false (default), per-request storage overrides are ignored. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers — see allow_per_request_raw_override.

logging_headers.description: List of headers to capture in log metadata

is_vk_mandatory.description: Whether virtual key (x-bf-vk header) is mandatory for all requests

required_headers.description: List of headers that must be present in requests

config.description: Configuration for the semantic cache plugin

provider.description: Provider to use for generating embeddings. Required for semantic search; omit it for direct hash mode with dimension: 1.

embedding_model.description: Model to use for generating embeddings in provider-backed semantic caching. Required when provider is set and not allowed in direct-only mode.

ttl.description: Time-to-live for cached responses (supports duration strings like '5m', '1h' or seconds as number, default: 5min)

threshold.description: Cosine similarity threshold for semantic matching (default: 0.8)

dimension.description: Dimension for vector store embeddings. Use 1 for direct (hash-based) caching without an embedding provider.

default_cache_key.description: Default cache key used when no per-request key is provided. When set, all requests without an explicit x-bf-cache-key header will use this value and be cached automatically.

conversation_history_threshold.description: Skip caching for requests with more than this number of messages in conversation history (default: 3)

cache_by_model.description: Include model in cache key (default: true)

cache_by_provider.description: Include provider in cache key (default: true)

exclude_system_prompt.description: Exclude system prompt in cache key (default: false)

Off by default: a replayed tool call runs in a later caller's agent loop with arguments chosen for someone else's prompt.

disable_identity_scoping.description: Share cache entries across identities. Off by default: an entry is only served to the identity that wrote it, meaning the same virtual key and the same user, even when requests share a cache key or default_cache_key. Set to true to let every identity share entries by cache key.

service_name.description: Name of the service to report to Datadog (can use env. prefix)

dogstatsd_addr.description: Combined host:port address of the DogStatsD server for metrics (agent mode only, can use env. prefix). Overridden by dogstatsd_host when set.

dogstatsd_host.description: Host of the DogStatsD server for metrics, provided separately from the port (agent mode only, can use env. prefix). Takes precedence over dogstatsd_addr when set. Useful in Kubernetes where the host is injected via the downward API (status.hostIP).

dogstatsd_port.description: Port of the DogStatsD server for metrics (agent mode only, can use env. prefix). Used only when dogstatsd_host is set (defaults to 8125); has no effect when dogstatsd_host is unset, in which case dogstatsd_addr supplies the port.

env.description: Environment tag (e.g., production, staging, can use env. prefix)

version.description: Service version tag (can use env. prefix)

custom_tags.description: Additional tags to add to all traces and metrics (values can use env. prefix)

metric_dimensions.description: Names of x-bf-dim-* request dimensions to forward as DogStatsD metric tags (e.g. ["team", "environment"]). disable_content_logging.description: Disable logging of message content to Datadog (default: false)

agentless.description: Use agentless mode to send data directly to Datadog APIs (default: false)
