request_headers.description: Request-header name patterns (exact or wildcard like "x-custom-*") whose values are stored in the request_headers column

config.description: Configuration for the Kafka traces plugin (Enterprise). Publishes completed traces as JSON messages to a Kafka topic, keyed by trace ID.

topic.description: Kafka topic to publish traces to (required)

sasl_enabled.description: Enable SASL authentication. SASL is only activated when both sasl_enabled is true and sasl is set.

sasl.description: SASL credentials, used when sasl_enabled is true

username.description: SASL username. Supports env var syntax: "env.MY_VAR".

password.description: SASL password. Supports env var syntax: "env.MY_VAR".

ca_cert.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate used to verify the broker's TLS certificate. Omit to use the system CA pool. Supports env var syntax: "env.KAFKA_CA_CERT".

batch_size.description: Maximum number of messages batched per write

flush_interval_ms.description: Maximum time (ms) to wait before flushing a batch

auto_create_topic.description: Create the topic at startup if it does not exist

disable_content_logging.description: Strip input/output message content from traces before publishing

request_headers.description: Request-header name patterns (exact or wildcard like "x-custom-*") whose captured values are embedded in published traces

config.description: Configuration for the Google Cloud Pub/Sub traces plugin (Enterprise). Publishes completed traces as JSON messages to a Pub/Sub topic.

topic_id.description: Pub/Sub topic ID — just the ID, not the full resource name (required)

service_account_key.description: Service account key JSON for authentication. Omit to use Application Default Credentials (ADC). Supports env var syntax: "env.MY_VAR".

auto_create_topic.description: Create the topic at startup if it does not exist

disable_content_logging.description: Strip request/response content from traces before publishing

request_headers.description: Request-header name patterns (exact or wildcard like "x-custom-*") whose captured values are included in published traces

relay_secret.description: A literal value, an env.VAR_NAME reference, or a structured secret reference (vault-backed secrets are stored as references).

relay_auth_config.description: How the endpoint's credential is presented to the upstream

type.description: bearer: Authorization: Bearer <key>; header: <header_name>: <value_prefix><key>; query: ?<query_param>=<key>; basic: Authorization: Basic base64(<key>) with the key as user:password; aws_sigv4: SigV4 with the endpoint's credential.aws; none: nothing injected (default bearer)

header_name.description: Header that carries the key (auth.type header)

query_param.description: Query parameter that carries the key (auth.type query)

value_prefix.description: Literal prefix placed before the key value (auth.type header)

service.description: SigV4 signing name, e.g. textract or translate. Requests are signed for credential.aws.region

relay_usage_config.description: Maps a relayed request/response onto usage and cost with gjson paths. Only the fields set are read. On the endpoint, a field left empty reads nothing; on a route, an empty field inherits the endpoint's value and reads nothing only when it is still empty after that (a route cannot switch an endpoint path off by leaving it blank). Negative numbers are ignored

model_path.description: Where the model name is read from the caller's request: a JSON body path (model, model_id), or the query parameter name with model_source query. Stored on the log row and checked against virtual-key model restrictions. Unset reads no model

model_source.description: Where model_path points: body (default), a JSON field of the request body; or query, a query parameter (Deepgram's ?model=nova-3)

input_tokens_path.description: Response body path for input tokens

output_tokens_path.description: Response body path for output tokens

total_tokens_path.description: Response body path for total tokens

cost_path.description: Response body path for an endpoint-reported USD cost; an array of numbers is summed

cost_per_request.description: Flat USD fee added to every billable call; on a route, 0 waives the endpoint fee

units_path.description: gjson path of the billable quantity, e.g. DocumentMetadata.Pages (response) or Text (request). Ignored when units_measure is body_bytes or body_chars

units_source.description: Body the quantity is read from: the upstream response (default) or the caller's request, which is what per-character APIs bill on

units_measure.description: value: the number at units_path (default); chars: the character count of the JSON string at units_path; body_bytes: the byte length of the whole body; body_chars: the character count of the whole body, any content type (what per-character APIs such as Azure Speech bill)

cost_per_unit.description: USD per unit; cost = units * cost_per_unit + cost_per_request + any extracted cost

units_block_size.description: Bill per started block of this many raw units: 100 for an API priced per 100 characters. Default exact

units_minimum.description: Least number of billed units once a quantity was read. Default 0

relay_streaming_config.description: Paths that are always relayed as streams. Otherwise a route's stream flag wins, and without one the upstream's reply decides: text/event-stream is streamed, anything else is read and priced. Nothing the caller sends selects streaming

paths.description: Rooted segment globs that always stream, e.g. /v1/stream/**

path.description: Rooted segment glob (* within a segment); a trailing /** matches the prefix and everything below

enabled.description: false refuses requests matching this route with 404, even when skip_route_check is on. Defaults to true

billable.description: false relays the call without counting or charging it; true counts it. Left unset, the method default applies, with or without a route: only POST is billable; GET and HEAD are polls and listings, PUT and PATCH update settings, DELETE cleans up

headers.description: Request headers that must also match for this route: header name (case-insensitive) to value glob. AWS JSON APIs send every operation to POST / and name it in X-Amz-Target, so one route per operation is {"X-Amz-Target": "Textract.GetDocumentAnalysis"} or a glob such as Textract.Get*

stream.description: Forces the streaming or buffered relay for this route

relay.description: A Relay: a raw HTTP relay to a non-LLM API served at /relay/{name}/{path}. Bifrost injects the relay's single credential, prices each counted call with the usage mapping (cost_per_request + cost_path + billed units x cost_per_unit, overridable per route) and charges the result to the caller's overall budgets. Virtual keys reach it through relay_grants.

base_url.description: Absolute http(s) upstream origin and base path every request is pinned under

credential.description: The one secret the endpoint signs in with: value for bearer, header, query and basic auth; aws for aws_sigv4. Omit for auth none.

extra_headers.description: Operator headers sent on every request; a caller cannot replace them

proxy_config.description: Outbound proxy; omit to inherit the global proxy when it is enabled for inference

routes.description: Upstream operations, first match wins; only listed routes are relayed unless skip_route_check is set

skip_route_check.description: Relay requests that match no route instead of refusing them with 404

ignore_upstream_cost.description: Ignore cost_path values; the operator's fee and unit pricing still apply

relay_name.description: Name of a relay this key may call

azure_storage_secret.description: A nonempty literal, env.VAR_NAME reference, or structured secret reference.

azure_object_storage.description: Azure Blob Storage. Supply a connection string, or a Blob service endpoint to use DefaultAzureCredential (including workload identity). Authentication is independent of inference-provider credentials.

endpoint.description: Azure Blob service URL for DefaultAzureCredential authentication. Mutually exclusive with connection_string. Supports env var and structured secret references.

connection_string.description: Azure Storage connection string. Mutually exclusive with endpoint. Supports env var and structured secret references.

mcp_max_protocol_version.description: An MCP protocol version cap: 'auto' (newest supported) or a revision.

warp_config.description: Warp settings (the dashboard's Settings > Warp page): the models Warp runs on, its behaviour and limits, log search, and topics. Takes the same body as PUT /api/warp/config and goes through the same validation and vector namespace provisioning. An omitted embedding, search or topic field keeps its stored value; every other omitted field takes its default, and additional_models is replaced whole. Under source_of_truth "split" it is applied when new or changed and dashboard edits are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is applied on every startup. Omit to manage Warp from the dashboard. The warp feature flag (feature_flags.flags.warp) is separate.

enabled.description: Show Warp in the dashboard. Requires a connected vector store, provider, model, embedding_provider, embedding_model and embedding_dimension.

provider.description: Provider of the default model that runs Warp's agent loop. Required when enabled.

model.description: Default model that runs Warp's agent loop. Required when enabled.

api_key_id.description: ID of one of the provider's configured keys to pin Warp to. Omit to load-balance across the provider's keys, or for a provider that needs no key.

additional_models.description: Other models people can switch to in the chat panel. Replaced whole: omitting it removes every additional model.

api_key_id.description: ID of one of the provider's configured keys to pin this model to

max_iterations.description: Tool-call rounds Warp may run before it must answer. 0 means the default; 1 is rejected because the last round is reserved for answering.

request_timeout_seconds.description: Deadline for each call to Warp's model. 0 means the default.

history_retention_days.description: How long a saved chat is kept after its last turn. 0 means the default. Independent of logs_store retention.

system_prompt_suffix.description: Text appended to Warp's built-in system prompt, such as naming conventions or cost model

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Omit to use the provider's default; 0 is fully deterministic.

reasoning_effort.description: Effort level for reasoning models. Omit for models that are not reasoning models.

embedding_provider.description: Provider of the model used to index and search logs. Required when enabled.

embedding_model.description: Model used to index and search logs. Required when enabled.

embedding_api_key_id.description: ID of one of the embedding provider's configured keys to pin embedding calls to

embedding_dimension.description: Vector size the embedding model returns, e.g. 1536 for text-embedding-3-small. Required when enabled.

log_vector_store_namespace.description: Vector store namespace holding Warp's log index. Must change whenever embedding_provider, embedding_model or embedding_dimension changes.

semantic_search_threshold.description: Minimum similarity for a semantic log search match. 0 resets it to the default; omitting it keeps the stored value.

semantic_search_limit.description: Most matches one semantic log search returns. 0 resets it to the default; omitting it keeps the stored value.

topic_discovery_min_requests.description: New topic threshold: how many requests that matched no topic must be waiting before Warp clusters them into new topics. Between 10 and 20000; 0 resets it to the default; omitting it keeps the stored value.

global_proxy_config.description: Global outbound proxy (the dashboard's proxy settings page) and which components use it. Under source_of_truth "split" it is applied when new or changed and dashboard edits are kept otherwise; under "config.json" it is applied on every startup. Omit to manage the proxy from the dashboard. Not the same as a provider's own proxy_config.

enabled.description: Turn the proxy on

type.description: Proxy type. Only http is supported.

url.description: Proxy URL, e.g. http://proxy.example.com:8080 (supports env.VAR_NAME). Required when enabled.

no_proxy.description: Comma-separated hosts that bypass the proxy: exact hosts, .example.com (domain and subdomains), *.example.com (subdomains), or *

skip_tls_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for the proxy

enable_for_scim.description: Enterprise: route SCIM directory sync and identity-provider requests through the proxy

enable_for_inference.description: Route inference requests through the proxy

enable_for_api.description: Route API requests through the proxy

definition.description: Replaces this tier's shipped definition. Omit to use the default.

signals.description: Replaces this tier's shipped signals. Omit to use the default.

examples.description: Replaces this tier's shipped examples. Omit to use the default.

plugin_span_filter.description: Controls which plugin hook spans this observability connector exports. Omit to export all plugin spans. Mode "include" exports only the listed plugins; mode "exclude" exports everything except them. Plugin names match the <name> in the span name "plugin.<name>.<stage>".

otel_profile_config.description: OpenTelemetry export profile. This legacy single-profile shape is still accepted directly as the plugin config.

enabled.description: Whether this profile exports traces and metrics

traces_enabled.description: Enable trace export for this profile. When false, no traces are sent and collector_url is not required, giving a metrics-only profile (pair with metrics_enabled).

service_name.description: Service name to be used for tracing

trace_type.description: Type of trace to use for the OTEL collector

protocol.description: Protocol to use for the OTEL collector

export_timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds for a single trace export. Bounds how long a slow or unreachable collector can hold an export goroutine; gRPC exports have no other timeout.

metrics_enabled.description: Enable push-based metrics export via OTLP. Recommended for multi-node cluster deployments.

metrics_endpoint.description: OTLP metrics endpoint URL (e.g., http://otel-collector:4318/v1/metrics for HTTP or otel-collector:4317 for gRPC)

overhead_breakdown_enabled.description: Export the per-component overhead histogram bifrost_overhead_component_microseconds (overhead latency split by the overhead_component attribute). Off by default. Requires metrics_enabled and an active trace, since the breakdown is computed from completed spans.

request_headers.description: Request header name patterns (exact or wildcard like x-custom-*) to capture and emit as span attributes. Note: * captures all headers including sensitive ones like Authorization.

disable_content_logging.description: When true, message content (input/output messages, embeddings, tool definitions, and tool call arguments/results) is dropped from exported spans. Only metadata such as model, tokens, and latency is sent to the collector.

excluded_attributes.description: Span attribute names to drop before export, matched exactly (e.g. "gen_ai.request.tools"). Unknown names are ignored.

export_raw_payloads.description: Attach the raw provider request/response bodies to LLM spans. Off by default: these carry provider-specific fields the normalized view does not. Guardrail redaction still applies. Also requires the provider's store_raw_request_response, and is suppressed by disable_content_logging. Bodies over 256 KB are dropped.

group_traces_by_session.description: When true, requests sharing the same x-bf-session-id header are grouped into a single OTEL trace, each request's root span appearing as a top-level sibling. An inbound W3C traceparent takes precedence, leaving that request on its own distributed trace.

disable_root_span_content.description: When true, input/output message content is dropped from the root span only; the underlying generation (llm.call) span retains the full content. This removes the duplicate input/output stored at the trace level (e.g. the Langfuse trace Input/Output goes empty) to reduce downstream storage.

headers.description: Custom headers sent to both the trace and metrics endpoints. Supports env.VAR_NAME prefix for environment variable substitution.

trace_headers.description: Extra headers sent only to the trace endpoint, overlaid on headers (same key wins). Supports env.VAR_NAME prefix.

metrics_headers.description: Extra headers sent only to the metrics endpoint, overlaid on headers (same key wins). Useful when a collector requires a per-signal header, e.g. a Databricks table name. Supports env.VAR_NAME prefix.

tls_ca_cert.description: Path to TLS CA certificate file

insecure.description: Skip TLS verification (ignored if tls_ca_cert is set)

otel_profiles_config.description: OpenTelemetry plugin configuration with one or more export profiles.

feature_flags_config.description: Boot-time overrides for feature flags. Flags themselves are declared in code via featureflags.Register; this block only sets initial values. Anything set here is rendered as locked in the UI - operators must edit the config (or Helm values) to change it.

enabled.description: Boolean value or a string: either 'env.NAME' for env-var indirection, or a literal boolean (true / false / 1 / 0 / yes / no / on / off, case-insensitive).

routing_fallback.description: A fallback in a routing rule's chain. Either the 'provider/model' string ('provider/' keeps the incoming model), or an object that additionally pins a provider key. A string must start with a provider and a slash: a bare provider name such as 'openai' names no provider and is skipped at request time.

model.description: Fallback model name. Omit to use the incoming request model

provider_key_name.description: Optional provider key name. Resolved to internal key_id at config load time. Requires provider.

key_id.description: Optional provider key ID to pin for this fallback. Not together with provider_key_name.

routing_target.description: A single weighted routing target within a rule. All fields except weight are optional; omitting provider or model means use the incoming request value. Weights across all targets in a rule must sum to 1.

provider.description: Target provider name (e.g., 'openai', 'azure'). Omit to use the incoming request provider

model.description: Target model name. Omit to use the incoming request model

provider_key_name.description: Optional provider key name. Resolved to internal key_id at config load time. Requires provider.

key_id.description: Optional provider key ID to pin for this target. Requires provider. Not together with provider_key_name.

weight.description: Probability weight for this target (must be > 0). All weights in a rule must sum to 1

ttft_timeout_ms.description: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) deadline in milliseconds for streaming requests routed to this target. An attempt that produces no first token in time is cut off and the next fallback runs. The last attempt is never cut off, so the setting only takes effect when fallbacks exist. Omit to disable.

routing_rule.description: Routing rule for dynamic provider/model selection

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled

cel_expression.description: CEL (Common Expression Language) expression for rule evaluation

chain_rule.description: If true, re-evaluates routing chain after this rule matches

targets.description: Weighted routing targets. Weights must sum to 1. Omit provider or model to use the incoming request value.

scope.description: Rule scope level. User-scoped rules can be created through the API and UI only: config.json does not support them, and a user-scoped rule in it is dropped at load with a warning.

scope_id.description: ID (not name) of the team, customer or virtual key. Required for non-global scopes; ignored for global. A new rule whose scope_id does not resolve is dropped at load with a warning; an edit that does not resolve keeps the stored rule, if the stored rule's own scope still resolves, and is dropped otherwise.

priority.description: Evaluation order within the rule's scope (scope plus scope_id); lower runs first. Must be unique within that scope, counting disabled rules and rules created in the UI or API. Defaults to 0, so two rules in one scope that both omit priority collide, and Bifrost exits at startup with 'routing rule with priority 0 already exists for scope ...'. Give every rule that shares a scope its own priority.

query.description: Visual rule builder state for the management UI (react-querybuilder). Omitted unless exported from the dashboard. Not evaluated at routing runtime (cel_expression is). When present, must include combinator and rules[] so arbitrary metadata cannot be mistaken for builder state.

rules.description: Leaf rules (field, operator, value) and/or nested combinator+rules groups from the query builder.

virtual_key_provider_config.description: Provider configuration for a virtual key

weight.description: Weight for load balancing (null opts out of weighted routing)

allowed_models.description: Allowed models for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all models; empty array denies all (deny-by-default). An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

blacklisted_models.description: Models blocked for this provider config even if matched by allowed_models. Use ["*"] to block all; empty array blocks none. An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

key_ids.description: Key identifiers allowed for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all keys. Semantics depend on version: v2 (default) empty = deny all; v1 empty = allow all. Values are the key IDs.

virtual_key_agent_grant.description: Agent grant for a virtual key

agent_name.description: Registered agent name granted to this virtual key

virtual_key_mcp_config.description: MCP configuration for a virtual key

mcp_client_name.description: MCP client name (config file format — resolved to mcp_client_id at startup)

tools_to_execute.description: Include-only list of tools this Virtual Key is permitted to execute from this MCP client. ['*'] means all tools allowed, [] means no tools allowed (deny-by-default).

complexity_tier_boundaries.description: Lexical score thresholds. simple_medium and medium_complex are applied by the complexity analyzer; complex_reasoning is retired and accepted for backward compatibility only.

simple_medium.description: Active lexical boundary applied by the complexity analyzer: a request scoring below this classifies as SIMPLE.

medium_complex.description: Active lexical boundary applied by the complexity analyzer: a request scoring below this classifies as MEDIUM, and at or above it as COMPLEX. Must remain greater than simple_medium when supplied, both for the analyzer and for backward compatibility.

complex_reasoning.description: Retired REASONING-tier boundary. Accepted for backward compatibility but ignored because REASONING is merged into COMPLEX.

complexity_analyzer_keywords.description: User-editable keyword scoring signals. The legacy four-list shape remains accepted for config.json compatibility. When the semantic block is present, the three normalized tier lists may contain at most 750 phrases combined; additive config.json merges are checked against that combined limit.

code_keywords.description: Deprecated legacy field. Values are merged into medium_keywords.

reasoning_keywords.description: Deprecated legacy field. Values are migrated to complex_keywords.

technical_keywords.description: Deprecated legacy field. Values are merged into medium_keywords.

complexity_analyzer_config.description: Runtime configuration for complexity_tier CEL routing with semantic or decision-model classification

classifier.description: Primary complexity classifier. Defaults to semantic.

allOf.description: Selecting the llm fallback without configuring the classifier it names loads a semantic classifier whose non-answers have nothing to fall back to; the loader rejects it for the same reason.

complexity_session_config.description: Session-aware complexity routing. When enabled and a supported session identity is present, Bifrost retains the highest tier observed across normally sequential turns for 24 hours of inactivity. The configured primary classifier supplies tiers; overlapping requests are best-effort.

enabled.description: Enable monotonic session tier retention; default false.

complexity_semantic_config.description: Embedding-based (semantic) complexity classification settings. Presence of this block enables the semantic classifier. The classifier embeds the analyzer's shared per-tier keyword lists as its exemplars.

provider.description: Provider used to generate embeddings for complexity classification

embedding_model.description: Model used to generate embeddings for complexity classification

timeout.description: Per-request embedding timeout (duration string like '1.5s' or '1500ms', or milliseconds as a number; default: 1500ms). Zero, in either form, means the default. On timeout no complexity tier is published and the request is recorded as 'skipped'.

min_similarity.description: Similarity floor a nearest-exemplar match must clear before its tier is used; a match below it publishes no tier and is recorded as 'skipped' (default: 0, meaning the nearest exemplar always wins however unrelated it is). Compared against the backend's own score: chromem, Qdrant, Pinecone, and Redis report raw cosine similarity, Weaviate reports certainty ((cosine+1)/2), so retune when switching backends.

message_history_count.description: How many of the most recent user messages are combined (oldest first) into the text that gets embedded (default: 1, the latest message only). Higher values let a short follow-up inherit the intent of earlier turns, at the cost of diluting the latest message and embedding more input tokens per request. Only user turns count; system prompts and assistant replies are never embedded.

count_toward_budgets.description: Record classification embedding cost against governance budgets (record-only, never enforced; default: false)

vector_store.description: Where exemplar embeddings are stored: 'embedded' uses the built-in chromem store, 'vector_store' uses the store configured in the top-level vector_store section and falls back to embedded when none is configured (default: embedded)

fallback.description: What answers when semantic classification produces no tier: none (default), the configured llm classifier, or the configured decision model.

complexity_llm_config.description: Chat-completion (LLM) fallback classifier settings. The block is inert unless complexity_semantic_config.fallback selects 'llm'; the classifier runs only after semantic classification produces no tier. Tier names (SIMPLE, MEDIUM, COMPLEX) and the response format are fixed: the gateway always appends a non-editable reinforcement stating them.

provider.description: Provider used to run the classification chat completion

model.description: Chat model asked to name the tier. Every fallback classification waits on one completion from this model, so pick a small, fast one.

timeout.description: Per-request classification timeout (duration string like '2s' or milliseconds as a number; default: 4s). Zero, in either form, means the default. On timeout no complexity tier is published and the request is recorded as 'skipped'.

prompt.description: Replaces the shipped classification guidance (max 4000 characters); empty means the shipped guidance is used. The tier-name and response-format reinforcement is appended by the gateway either way and cannot be edited.

message_history_count.description: How many of the most recent user messages are given to the classifier, oldest first (default: 1, the latest message only). Only user turns count; system prompts and assistant replies are never sent.

count_toward_budgets.description: Record classification completion cost against governance budgets (record-only, never enforced; default: false)

auth_config.description: Authentication configuration. Deprecated: Use governance.auth_config instead.

disable_auth_on_inference.description: Deprecated and ignored. Use client_config.enforce_auth_on_inference instead.

pricing_sync_interval.description: Pricing sync interval in seconds. Default is 24 hours. Minimum is 3600 seconds (1 hour).

mcp_library_url.description: URL to a custom MCP server catalog. Leave empty to use the default Bifrost catalog. In config.json this also accepts a file:// URL to load the catalog from local disk in air-gapped deployments; the API accepts http(s) URLs only.

mcp_library_sync_interval.description: MCP library sync interval in seconds. Set to 0 to disable background catalog syncing entirely (air-gapped deployments with no local catalog file); an explicit force-sync still works. Default is 24 hours; minimum when enabled is 3600 seconds (1 hour).

live_models_sync_interval.description: How often each provider's list-models response is re-fetched in the background, in seconds. Without this, a model an upstream starts serving after the gateway booted stays invisible until a restart or a key edit. Set to 0 to disable background refresh. Default is 1 hour; minimum when enabled is 60 seconds.

base_url.description: Base URL for the provider (optional, required for Ollama). Management API updates accept an origin and optional path, without credentials, query parameters, or fragments.

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to send with requests. A value may be a literal, an env.VAR_NAME reference, or a vault.path reference; references are resolved at load time and only the reference is stored. Literal values are masked in API responses while env/vault references stay visible as references; on update, a masked value sent back under the same header name keeps the stored value, while a masked value under a new or renamed header, or on provider create, is rejected with 400.

default_request_timeout_in_seconds.description: Default request timeout in seconds. For streaming requests this bounds the connection, the request write and the wait for response headers; once headers arrive, stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds governs the body.

enforce_http2.description: Force HTTP/2 on provider connections (relevant for Bedrock and other net/http-based providers)

http2_ping_interval_in_seconds.description: Seconds of stream idle before a client-initiated HTTP/2 keepalive PING (0 = disabled; only when enforce_http2).

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA). Supports inline PEM or env.VAR_NAME.

stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle timeout per stream chunk in seconds. If no data is received for this many seconds, the stream is closed. Default: 120.

keep_alive_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle keep-alive for pooled connections, in seconds. Set below the upstream server's keep-alive so Bifrost drops idle connections before the server closes them. Default: 30.

max_conns_per_host.description: Maximum number of TCP connections per provider host. For HTTP/2 (e.g. Bedrock), each connection supports ~100 concurrent streams. Default: 5000.

beta_header_overrides.description: Override default beta header support per provider. For Anthropic-family providers, keys are anthropic-beta prefixes (e.g. 'redact-thinking-'); for TypeSafe-based providers, 'typesafe-danger-zone-images' controls the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images header sent with image and box requests. Values are true (supported) or false (unsupported). Headers not listed use the built-in defaults.

allow_private_network.description: Allow connections to RFC 1918 private IPs (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x). Enable for providers on a k8s pod network, LAN, or private VPC. Loopback addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) remain allowed regardless of this setting. Link-local addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to send with requests. A value may be a literal, an env.VAR_NAME reference, or a vault.path reference; references are resolved at load time and only the reference is stored. Literal values are masked in API responses while env/vault references stay visible as references; on update, a masked value sent back under the same header name keeps the stored value, while a masked value under a new or renamed header, or on provider create, is rejected with 400.

default_request_timeout_in_seconds.description: Default request timeout in seconds. For streaming requests this bounds the connection, the request write and the wait for response headers; once headers arrive, stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds governs the body.

enforce_http2.description: Force HTTP/2 on provider connections (relevant for Bedrock and other net/http-based providers)

http2_ping_interval_in_seconds.description: Seconds of stream idle before a client-initiated HTTP/2 keepalive PING (0 = disabled; only when enforce_http2).

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA)

stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle timeout per stream chunk in seconds. If no data is received for this many seconds, the stream is closed. Default: 120.

keep_alive_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle keep-alive for pooled connections, in seconds. Set below the upstream server's keep-alive so Bifrost drops idle connections before the server closes them. Default: 30.

max_conns_per_host.description: Maximum number of TCP connections per provider host. For HTTP/2 (e.g. Bedrock), each connection supports ~100 concurrent streams. Default: 5000.

beta_header_overrides.description: Override default beta header support per provider. For Anthropic-family providers, keys are anthropic-beta prefixes (e.g. 'redact-thinking-'); for TypeSafe-based providers, 'typesafe-danger-zone-images' controls the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images header sent with image and box requests. Values are true (supported) or false (unsupported). Headers not listed use the built-in defaults.

allow_private_network.description: Allow connections to RFC 1918 private IPs (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x). Enable for providers on a k8s pod network, LAN, or private VPC. Loopback addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) remain allowed regardless of this setting. Link-local addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.

openai_config.description: OpenAI Responses API settings, honoured by the openai and fireworks providers

disable_store.description: Force store=false on outgoing Responses API requests (openai and fireworks).

cache_control_injection_point.description: One place to add a cache breakpoint. Must set role, index, or both; a point with neither matches nothing.

location.description: What to target. Only conversation messages are supported today.

index.description: Match the message at this position. Negative values count from the end, so -1 is the last message. An index past either end matches nothing.

prompt_cache.description: Synthesize prompt-cache breakpoints for requests that carry none. Off by default. Agentic clients such as Codex send no cache markers, so providers that cache implicitly slide the cached prefix onto the latest message and bill a cache write every turn. Requests that already carry their own cache_control or prompt_cache_breakpoint are never modified.

auto_inject.description: Mark the first cacheable content block. That block is the prefix an agent loop replays verbatim each turn, so the cached region stays stable and turn 2 onward is a cache read.

ttl.description: Lifetime for injected markers. Omit for the provider default (5 minutes on Anthropic). Providers that cannot carry a TTL ignore it.

cache_control_injection_points.description: Target specific messages instead of the first cacheable block. When set, this REPLACES auto_inject rather than adding to it. At most four markers are injected, matching the Anthropic ceiling.

injected_tools.description: MCP tools Bifrost injects into every chat and responses request served by this provider and executes server side when the model calls them. The client never sees the injected tool call, only the final answer. Names must be unique within a provider.

name.description: Tool name the model sees. It replaces any client tool with the same name; the name web_search also replaces native web search tools and web_search_options.

mcp_client_name.description: Name of the configured MCP client that provides the tool

tool_name.description: Tool name as the MCP server exposes it, without the client prefix

passthrough_policy.description: Routes the HTTP relays (/openai_passthrough, /anthropic_passthrough, /azure_passthrough, /genai_passthrough, /bedrock_passthrough) forward to this provider. Omit to use the default: a built-in provider forwards every route, a custom provider forwards none. An empty allowed_routes forwards nothing. A custom provider is reached on its base provider's route with the x-model-provider header, once it has a policy.

allowed_routes.description: Routes forwarded to the provider. A request is forwarded when any rule allows it.

passthrough_route_rule.description: One allowed route: a path with optional methods.

methods.description: HTTP methods the rule allows. Omit to allow any method.

path.description: Path after the route prefix, as the client calls it. * matches within one segment; a final /** matches the path and everything below it.

value.description: API key value (can use env. prefix)

oauth_key_config.description: OAuth-minted bearer for OpenAI-compatible providers, including custom providers built on the openai base. Set this and leave value empty: Bifrost mints the access token from the token endpoint, caches it per credential and refreshes it before expiry. A non-empty value always wins.

grant_type.description: client_credentials (RFC 6749 §4.4) or jwt_bearer (RFC 7523: Bifrost signs an assertion with private_key).

token_url.description: Token endpoint, absolute https URL (plain http is accepted for loopback hosts only; can use env. prefix). Must not carry userinfo, a query or a fragment; send extra parameters through extra_params.

client_id.description: client_credentials: client ID (can use env. prefix)

client_secret.description: client_credentials: client secret (can use env. prefix)

private_key.description: jwt_bearer: RSA or EC private key in PEM form (can use env. prefix)

audience.description: jwt_bearer: aud claim (required); client_credentials: optional audience form parameter

key_id.description: jwt_bearer: kid header, when the server selects keys by id

auth_style.description: client_credentials: send the client credentials as HTTP Basic auth (header) or as form fields (body)

extra_params.description: Extra form parameters sent on the token request

assertion_lifetime_seconds.description: jwt_bearer: seconds from issue until the assertion expires (exp = now + value); 0 or omitted uses the default of 300. iat is backdated by 30 seconds for clock skew, so the assertion's exp - iat span is this value plus 30.

models.description: Models this key can access. Use ["*"] to allow all models; empty array denies all (deny-by-default). An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

enabled.description: Whether this key is used for routing. Set to false to keep the key configured but skip it during key selection. New keys default to true; omitting it on an existing key keeps the stored value

use_for_batch_api.description: Whether this key can be used for batch API operations (default: false)

oneOf.description: Legacy shape: a bare provider-specific identifier. Equivalent to {"model_id": "<value>"}.
