agent_upstream_auth.description: Authentication for upstream A2A agent requests. Secret values support env.<VAR> and vault.<key> references.

headers.description: Headers to attach (for type 'headers'). Values can use env. or vault. prefix.

client_id.description: OAuth client ID (can use env. or vault. prefix).

client_secret.description: OAuth client secret (can use env. or vault. prefix).

security_schemes.description: Agent Card security scheme names this auth satisfies.

endpoint_slug.description: URL-safe, immutable slug that serves this client at /mcp/<slug>. Derived from the name when omitted; must be unique across MCP clients and Virtual MCPs.

is_code_mode_client.description: Whether this client is a code mode client

connection_type.description: Connection type for MCP client. 'openapi' synthesizes an in-process MCP server from an OpenAPI/Swagger document (see openapi_config); its tools proxy HTTP calls to the described API.

openapi_config.description: Configuration for connection_type 'openapi'. At least one of spec (inline JSON/YAML text), spec_file (path relative to the config directory, read at load) or spec_url (fetched at every connect) supplies the document, in that order of precedence; the others then record where it came from. Supported documents: Swagger 2.0, OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2.

spec.description: Inline OpenAPI/Swagger document (JSON or YAML text).

spec_file.description: Path to the document, relative to the config.json directory (or absolute). Read once at load; the content is what gets persisted.

spec_url.description: http(s) URL of the document. Fetched at connect time when spec and spec_file are not given; next to spec it records the source and resolves relative servers.

base_url.description: Upstream API base URL. Defaults to the document's first server entry; required when the document declares none or only relative ones.

security_credentials.description: Credentials keyed by the document's securitySchemes name. apiKey and http-bearer schemes take value; http-basic takes username and password. Values support env.VAR and vault.path references.

include_deprecated.description: Expose operations the document marks deprecated.

max_response_bytes.description: Cap on the upstream response body returned to the model (0 = default 64 KiB).

connection_string.description: HTTP or SSE URL (alternative to http_config sub-object, required for HTTP or SSE connections)

token_exchange.description: Delegated token-exchange configuration for auth_type 'token_exchange': each caller's identity-provider token is exchanged at runtime for a short-lived token scoped to this server's audience. The exchange endpoint and grant shape come from the deployment's identity-provider integration; the application performing the exchange is configured here. Requires user-identity authentication to be available. The MCP client lands in `pending_verification` state at boot; an admin verifies it once from the UI (as themselves).

audience.description: Resource identifier the exchanged token is scoped to at the identity provider (e.g. 'api://jira-mcp')

use_idp_credentials.description: When true, performs the exchange as the SSO login application itself instead of client_id/client_secret below, which are then ignored. Always implied by the id_jag profile, since the identity provider accepts the user's sign-in token only from the app it was issued to. Some providers require this: Microsoft Entra ID's on-behalf-of grant only accepts an assertion audienced to the exchanging application, and Bifrost's SSO login flow always requests a token self-audienced to the SSO application, so a separate exchange application can never receive a usable one.

client_id.description: Identity-provider application authorized to perform exchanges for this audience — typically a dedicated registration carrying the token-exchange (or on-behalf-of) grant, separate from the SSO login application. Required unless use_idp_credentials is true. Can use env. or vault. prefix.

client_secret.description: Secret for the exchange application; omit for public clients. Ignored when use_idp_credentials is true. Can use env. or vault. prefix.

authorization_server_url.description: Overrides where the exchange request is sent, for identity providers that bind an audience to a specific authorization server distinct from the one used for SSO login (e.g. Okta's per-resource Custom Authorization Servers). Leave empty to use the deployment's SSO login issuer, which is correct for providers with one tenant-wide token endpoint (Entra, Auth0). Takes an issuer URL, from which the token endpoint is derived, or a full token endpoint URL ending in /token, which is used as is.

scopes.description: Optional scopes to request on the exchanged token. Include 'offline_access' (where the identity provider supports it) so exchanges issue refresh tokens, keeping the retained admin discovery credential self-renewing.

profile.description: Empty (default): the identity provider issues the upstream token directly. 'id_jag' (Bifrost Enterprise): Cross App Access (Okta XAA) — the identity provider issues an ID-JAG for `audience` (the upstream authorization server's issuer) from the user's SSO session, and the upstream authorization server exchanges it for its own token with the jwt-bearer grant. Users must have signed in to Bifrost through the identity provider.

resource.description: id_jag only: resource indicator sent to the identity provider. Set it only when the identity provider's connection defines one; Okta rejects a resource it does not expect. Omitted when empty.

resource_token_endpoint.description: id_jag only: the upstream authorization server's token endpoint. Defaults to the endpoint discovered from the audience's own authorization server metadata (never from what the MCP server advertises), whose issuer must equal the audience and which must list the jwt-bearer grant.

resource_client_id.description: id_jag only, required: Bifrost's client ID registered at the upstream authorization server. Can use env. or vault. prefix.

resource_client_secret.description: id_jag only: secret for resource_client_id; omit for a public client or when resource_private_key is set. Can use env. or vault. prefix.

resource_private_key.description: id_jag only: PEM RSA or EC private key. When set, Bifrost authenticates to the upstream authorization server with private_key_jwt (a client assertion signed with this key, audience the token endpoint) instead of a client secret. Cannot be combined with resource_client_secret. Can use env. or vault. prefix.

resource_key_id.description: id_jag only: kid header of the client assertion, when the upstream server selects keys by ID. Requires resource_private_key.

resource_signing_algorithm.description: id_jag only: client assertion signing algorithm; empty (default) means RS256. Use an ES algorithm with an EC key. Requires resource_private_key.

resource_assertion_audience.description: id_jag only: aud claim of the client assertion. Defaults to the upstream token endpoint, which Okta and Entra require; set the authorization server's issuer for servers that expect it instead. Requires resource_private_key.

resource_client_auth_method.description: id_jag only: how resource_client_secret is sent. Empty (default) uses HTTP Basic unless the discovered metadata admits only client_secret_post. Set it when resource_token_endpoint is configured, since there is then no discovery. Requires resource_client_secret.

allOf.$comment: Bifrost authenticates to the upstream authorization server with a client secret or a private key, not both.
The id_jag profile redeems the ID-JAG as a client of the upstream authorization server.
client_id is required unless use_idp_credentials is true or the profile is id_jag, in which cases the exchange uses the SSO login application's own credentials instead.

oauth_config.description: Inline OAuth provider configuration for auth_type 'oauth' or 'per_user_oauth'. All inner fields are optional — missing URLs are resolved via RFC 8414 discovery and a missing client_id triggers RFC 7591 dynamic client registration at admin-click time. The client lands in `pending_verification` state at boot; an admin runs the verification flow once from the MCP Gateway UI.

client_id.description: OAuth client ID (optional — Dynamic Client Registration is used when omitted; can use env. or vault. prefix)

client_secret.description: OAuth client secret (optional — omit for PKCE public clients or DCR; can use env. or vault. prefix)

authorize_url.description: Provider authorize endpoint (optional — discovered from the MCP server URL when omitted)

token_url.description: Provider token endpoint (optional — discovered when omitted)

registration_url.description: Dynamic Client Registration endpoint (optional — discovered when omitted)

resource.description: OAuth resource indicator, RFC 8707 (optional: discovered from the MCP server's protected resource metadata when omitted)

use_client_metadata_document.description: Register with Bifrost's Client ID Metadata Document even if the authorization server does not advertise support (for example when discovery fails and the endpoints are entered by hand). Requires Bifrost on a public HTTPS address; cannot be combined with client_id. When off, the document is still used automatically wherever the server advertises support.

per_user_header_keys.description: Required header names each end-user must supply when auth_type is 'per_user_headers'. Schema only — values are submitted per-user at runtime. The MCP client lands in `pending_verification` state at boot; an admin submits sample values once from the UI to verify the connection and discover tools.

headers.description: Headers to send with the request (for headers auth type)

tools_to_execute.description: Include-only list of tools to execute. ['*'] means all, [] means none.

tools_to_auto_execute.description: Auto-execute list of tools. ['*'] means all, [] means none.

prompts_to_expose.description: Prompts (by the server's own name) served through Bifrost's MCP gateway. ['*'] for all, [] for none. Omitted, a new server serves all and an existing one keeps its stored list.

resources_to_expose.description: Resource URIs and URI templates served through Bifrost's MCP gateway. ['*'] for all, [] for none. Omitted, a new server serves all and an existing one keeps its stored list.

max_protocol_version.description: Per-client cap on the MCP protocol version Bifrost offers this server. Omit to use the global mcp.max_protocol_version; 'auto' uses the newest version Bifrost supports.

tool_sync_interval.description: Per-client override for tool sync interval as a Go duration string in whole seconds (e.g. '10m', '90s'; '0s' or omitted = use global). Legacy integer nanoseconds are also accepted and must be a whole number of seconds.

tool_execution_timeout.description: Per-client override for tool execution timeout. Accepts a Go duration string (e.g. '30s', '2m') or a bare integer treated as seconds. When set, overrides the global tool_manager_config.tool_execution_timeout for this MCP server only. Omit or set to 0 to use the global default.

max_instructions_length.description: Per-client override for the forwarded instruction byte cap. When set, overrides the global mcp.tool_manager_config.max_instructions_per_client for this MCP server only; the aggregate is still bounded by max_instructions_total. Omit or set to 0 to use the global default.

allowed_extra_headers.description: Allowlist of request-level headers that callers may forward to this MCP server at execution time. Use ['*'] to allow all headers.

is_ping_available.description: Whether the MCP server supports ping for health checks (default: true)

needs_session_stickiness.description: Only meaningful for connection_type 'http': whether this client maintains one persistent connection reused across every caller (true) or connects fresh per call (false, the default for newly created clients). SSE and STDIO always behave as sticky regardless of this field.

require_public_target.description: Server-managed. Set to true when the client was registered over the management API with no admin credential check; every connection to the MCP server (initial, reconnect, per-call) must then resolve to a public address. Once stored as true it is never cleared by the API or by config.json reconciliation; declaring it true here is honored.

per_user_discovery.description: Only valid for per-user auth types (per_user_oauth, per_user_headers, token_exchange): when true, each caller's discovery (its tool list and the server's instructions) is made with its own credential and kept per (auth mode, identity, client), and the client stores no admin credential and does no admin discovery. When false, every caller is served the discovery made with the admin credential. Not supported yet — reserved; setting it is currently rejected.

tool_pricing.description: Tool pricing map (tool name to cost per execution)

allow_by_default.description: When true, this MCP server is available to every caller that has not been assigned it explicitly, with all tools allowed. An explicit assignment for a caller takes precedence over this setting for that caller.

allow_on_all_virtual_keys.description: Deprecated: use allow_by_default. Read only when allow_by_default is absent.

disabled.description: When true, this MCP client is disabled (connection and workers are stopped while preserving configuration).

tls_config.description: TLS configuration for HTTP and SSE connections. Not applicable to stdio or inprocess connection types.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable TLS certificate verification. Takes priority over ca_cert_pem when both are set. Use only in development or trusted isolated environments. Not recommended for production.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for MCP server connections. Use when the MCP server uses a self-signed or private CA certificate. Supports env.VAR_NAME syntax to read the certificate from an environment variable.

allOf.$comment: per_user_headers requires the admin to declare which header names users must submit. OAuth-based types have no required input — the connection_string drives RFC 8414 discovery + RFC 7591 dynamic client registration when oauth_config is omitted or its inner fields are blank.

oauth_config only applies to OAuth-based auth types; forbid it elsewhere (including entries that omit auth_type, which defaults to headers) so a misplaced block fails validation instead of being silently ignored.
per_user_header_keys only applies to auth_type 'per_user_headers'; forbid it elsewhere so a misplaced declaration fails validation instead of being silently ignored.
token_exchange requires its scoping block (audience), and the block only applies to that auth type; forbid it elsewhere so a misplaced declaration fails validation instead of being silently ignored.
openapi_config only applies to connection_type 'openapi'; forbid it elsewhere so a misplaced block fails validation instead of being silently ignored.
A synthesized OpenAPI server has no remote MCP handshake to authenticate: only none, headers and per_user_headers apply. OAuth-flavored and token-exchange auth types are refused.

tool_execution_timeout.description: Tool execution timeout. Accepts a duration string (e.g. "30s", "2m") or an integer number of seconds (e.g. 30 means 30 seconds).

code_mode_binding_level.description: How tools are exposed in VFS for code execution

disable_auto_tool_inject.description: When true, MCP tools are not automatically injected into requests. Tools are only included when explicitly specified via request context filters or headers, such as x-bf-mcp-include-tools or x-bf-mcp-include-clients.

max_instructions_per_client.description: Byte bound on a single MCP server's forwarded instructions. Longer text is truncated on a rune boundary with a notice. 0 uses the built-in default of 4096.

max_instructions_total.description: Byte bound on the whole forwarded aggregate across every visible MCP server. Rides on every MCP-bearing request that carries tools, so raising it raises per-request tokens. 0 uses the built-in default of 16384.

oauth_private_allowlist.description: Hostnames, IP addresses, or CIDR ranges (no schemes or ports) that the MCP OAuth chain (discovery, dynamic client registration, token requests) may reach even when they resolve to a loopback or private address. Applies only to MCP clients registered by an authenticated admin or declared in config.json; clients registered while dashboard auth was off stay public-only. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are always refused and cannot be listed. Example: ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "10.20.0.0/16"].

mcp_code_mode_limits.description: Limits applied to each code mode (executeToolCode) execution. Every field is optional; omit it or set 0 to use the built-in default. There is no limit on how many executions run concurrently.

max_source_bytes.description: Maximum size of the submitted code in bytes. 0 uses the default of 65536 (64 KiB).

max_steps.description: Maximum interpreter computation steps per execution, including work inside builtins. 0 uses the default of 1000000.

max_memory_bytes.description: Estimated allocation budget per execution in bytes, enforced by the interpreter and value converters before allocating. 0 uses the default of 67108864 (64 MiB).

max_log_bytes.description: Maximum print and tool log output per execution in bytes, including newlines. 0 uses the default of 65536 (64 KiB).

max_tool_calls.description: Maximum nested MCP tool calls per execution. 0 uses the default of 64.

max_value_bytes.description: Size budget in bytes for each tool payload and converted result, counted conservatively for JSON escaping. Must be 0 (default of 1048576, 1 MiB) or at least 1024.

max_nesting_depth.description: Maximum nesting depth of values crossing the tool boundary. 0 uses the default of 64; at most 1000.

virtual_mcp_config.description: A Virtual MCP: a named bundle of tools from one or more MCP clients, served at /mcp/<endpoint_slug> and attachable to virtual keys.

id.description: DB ID of this Virtual MCP. When set, the reconciler updates the existing Virtual MCP with this ID rather than matching by name.

endpoint_slug.description: URL-safe path the Virtual MCP is served at (/mcp/<endpoint_slug>). Honored on create only (immutable after); derived from the name when omitted. Unique across Virtual MCPs and MCP clients.

enabled.description: Whether the Virtual MCP is enabled. A disabled Virtual MCP is not served.

tools.description: Per-client tool specs the Virtual MCP exposes

mcp_client_name.description: MCP client name (resolved to client_id at startup)

tool_names.description: Tool names to expose. ["*"] means all tools (including future ones); [] means none; a named list means only those tools.

virtual_key_ids.description: Virtual keys this Virtual MCP is attached to.

id.description: DB ID of this tool group. When set, the reconciler updates the existing group with this ID rather than matching by name.

enabled.description: Whether tool group is enabled

tools.description: MCP tools included in this group

mcp_client_name.description: MCP client name (resolved to client_id at startup)

tool_names.description: Tool names to expose. ["*"] means all tools (including future ones); [] means none; a named list means only those tools.

team_ids.description: DEPRECATED: attach Virtual MCPs to virtual keys via virtual_key_ids instead.

customer_ids.description: DEPRECATED: attach Virtual MCPs to virtual keys via virtual_key_ids instead.

user_ids.description: DEPRECATED: attach Virtual MCPs to virtual keys via virtual_key_ids instead.

provider_names.description: DEPRECATED: attach Virtual MCPs to virtual keys via virtual_key_ids instead.

api_key_ids.description: DEPRECATED: attach Virtual MCPs to virtual keys via virtual_key_ids instead.

scheme.description: Weaviate server scheme (http or https) - REQUIRED

host.description: Weaviate server host (host:port). If host is without a port number then the 80 port for insecured and 443 port for secured connections will be used.

secured.description: Secured set it to true if it's a secured connection

headers.description: Additional headers to send with requests

class_name.description: Class name for Weaviate vector store

redis_config.description: Redis configuration for vector store (also used for Valkey-compatible endpoints)

addr.description: Redis/Valkey server address (host:port) - REQUIRED (can use env. prefix)

username.description: Username for Redis AUTH (optional, can use env. prefix)

password.description: Password for Redis AUTH (optional, can use env. prefix)

use_tls.description: Use TLS for the Redis/Valkey connection (optional)

insecure_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for Redis/Valkey connections. Use only when a trusted CA cannot be configured.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for Redis/Valkey TLS connections

cluster_mode.description: Use Redis Cluster mode. Required for cluster configuration endpoints; when enabled, db must be 0.

host.description: Qdrant server host - REQUIRED (can use env. prefix)

api_key.description: API key for authentication (optional, can use env. prefix)

max_recv_msg_size_mb.description: gRPC max receive message size in MB (default: 64). Increase when caching large payloads such as base64-encoded image generation responses.

api_key.description: Pinecone API key - REQUIRED (can use env. prefix)

index_host.description: Index host URL from Pinecone console - REQUIRED (e.g., your-index.svc.environment.pinecone.io)

chromem_config.description: Embedded chromem configuration for vector store. Chromem runs in-process (pure Go, no external service), so its data lives on one node and is never shared between replicas, and every filtered read is a full scan of the namespace. Suited to small, node-local vector sets rather than a shared cache.

path.description: Directory for on-disk persistence, reloaded on startup. Must hold a non-whitespace value - omit the field entirely for a memory-only store that starts empty after every restart.

compress.description: Compress persisted documents on disk. Requires path - a memory-only store has nothing to compress.

url.description: URL of the proxy server (supports env.VAR_NAME or a literal URI)

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for TLS connections through the proxy (for SSL-intercepting proxies, and for the proxy itself when the URL is https://, supports env.VAR_NAME)

enabled.description: Whether cluster mode is enabled

type.description: Clustering mode. 'mesh' (default) is peer-to-peer via memberlist gossip. 'broker' routes all cluster traffic through a central broker process, for platforms without peer-to-peer connectivity (e.g. Cloud Run).

region.description: Region label for cluster deployment (runtime default: unknown)

failure_threshold.description: Number of failed probes before marking as failed

grpc.description: gRPC transport settings for the cluster counter-sync layer. Replaces the memberlist gossip broadcast path for governance usage counters; memberlist continues to handle cluster membership and other entity sync.

port.description: TCP port the gRPC server listens on

dial_timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait when dialing a peer, in seconds

enabled.description: Whether auto-discovery is enabled

service_name.description: Service name used for discovery (used by consul, etcd, UDP, and mDNS)

bind_port.description: Port to bind for cluster communication

dial_timeout.description: Timeout for discovery dial operations as a Go duration string (e.g. '5s', '1m')

allowed_address_space.description: CIDR notation for allowed address spaces (e.g., ['10.0.0.0/8', '192.168.0.0/16'])

k8s_label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector for filtering pods

dns_names.description: DNS names to resolve for node discovery. Supports env.VAR_NAME for environment variable substitution.

consul_address.description: Consul server address for service discovery

mdns_service.description: mDNS service name for local network discovery

broker.description: Broker settings, used when type is 'broker'

address.description: host:port of the broker that nodes dial

tls.description: Whether to dial the broker over TLS

auth_token.description: Optional shared secret sent on connect

listen_port.description: Port the broker process serves on (default: 50051)

scim_config.description: SAML/SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) configuration

enabled.description: Whether SAML/SCIM authentication is enabled

trusted_networks.description: Private IP/CIDR allowlist the SSRF guard consults before outbound discovery calls (the generic provider's discover-endpoints and discover-claims flows), so a self-hosted IdP on an internal network can be reached. Declaring this key makes config.json own the whole list: it replaces whatever is stored, and an explicit empty array clears dashboard-added entries. Omit the key to leave the stored allowlist untouched.

cidr.description: IP or CIDR range to trust, e.g. 10.20.0.0/16. A bare IP is treated as a single host (/32, or /128 for IPv6). Hostnames are not accepted, since DNS would then decide which requests bypass SSRF protection.

description.description: Optional admin-facing label for this range, e.g. On-prem Keycloak

authServerType.description: 'org' for Org Authorization Server or 'custom' for Custom Authorization Server. Auto-detected from issuer URL when omitted.

apiToken.description: Okta API token for Admin API access (optional; enables background user/group reconciliation on the bulkSyncInterval schedule, 24h by default)

syncAllUsers.description: Which Okta users directory sync (apiToken) keeps. True (the default when unset) syncs every app-assigned user except those SUSPENDED or DEPROVISIONED (deactivated); false syncs ACTIVE users only.

additionalScopes.description: Extra OAuth scopes requested on top of the base openid/profile/email/offline_access set. Primarily for Custom Authorization Servers where claims like 'groups' are gated behind a scope Bifrost does not request by default.

userIdField.description: JWT claim field for user ID (default: 'sub')

teamIdsField.description: JWT claim field for team IDs (default: 'groups')

entra_config.description: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) JWT authentication configuration

tenantId.description: Azure tenant ID or 'common' for multi-tenant applications

clientSecret.description: Client secret (optional, required for token revocation)

cloud.description: Cloud environment: 'commercial' (default), 'gcc-high' for US Government GCC High, or 'dod' for Department of Defense

appIdUri.description: App ID URI for v1.0 tokens (e.g., api://{clientId})

userIdField.description: JWT claim field for user ID (default: 'oid')

teamIdsField.description: JWT claim field for team IDs (default: 'groups')

enableBulkSync.description: Whether Bifrost may bulk-sync users and groups from Microsoft Graph. Set automatically by the SCIM verify step (disabled when the app registration is missing the required Graph permissions); set it explicitly to opt out of bulk sync while keeping login-time claim sync.

serverUrl.description: Base URL of the Keycloak server (e.g., https://keycloak.company.com). Must NOT include the /realms/{realm} suffix.

clientId.description: Keycloak client ID for the confidential client used by Bifrost

clientSecret.description: Keycloak client secret. Supports env. prefix for environment variable references (e.g., 'env.KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET')

userIdField.description: JWT claim field for user ID (default: 'sub')

teamIdsField.description: JWT claim field for team IDs (default: 'groups')

generic_config.description: Generic OIDC authentication configuration for any standards-compliant OIDC identity provider. Endpoints are resolved via OIDC discovery (.well-known/openid-configuration) from issuerUrl unless overridden.

clientSecret.description: OAuth2/OIDC client secret (optional, for confidential clients). Supports env. prefix for environment variable references.

authorizationEndpoint.description: Manual override for the authorization endpoint (used in preference to discovery when set)

tokenEndpoint.description: Manual override for the token endpoint (used in preference to discovery when set)

userinfoEndpoint.description: Manual override for the userinfo endpoint (used in preference to discovery when set)

teamIdsField.description: JWT claim field for team/group IDs (default: 'groups')

rolesField.description: JWT claim field for role names (optional)

scopes.description: Override the default OIDC scopes requested during login

displayName.description: Label for the login button ("Sign in with <displayName>"). Defaults to "SSO".

domain.description: Zitadel instance domain (e.g., 'my-instance.zitadel.cloud' or 'auth.company.com'). Bare host only - do NOT include the scheme, port, or path.

clientSecret.description: Zitadel client secret (optional, required for confidential clients and token revocation)

projectId.description: Optional Zitadel project ID for project-scoped role claims

serviceAccountClientId.description: Service account client ID for Zitadel Management API (required for user provisioning - web apps cannot use client_credentials)

serviceAccountClientSecret.description: Service account client secret for Zitadel Management API

teamIdsField.description: JWT claim field for team/group IDs (default: 'groups')

domain.description: Google Workspace primary domain (e.g., 'company.com'). Bare host only - do NOT include the scheme, port, or path.

clientSecret.description: Google client secret (optional, used for token revocation)

credentialMode.description: How Directory API credentials are sourced. 'inherit' uses Application Default Credentials; 'env' uses serviceAccountEnvVar; 'file' uses serviceAccountFile.

serviceAccountEnvVar.description: Name of the environment variable containing the service account JSON (used when credentialMode is 'env'). Required for Directory API access without ADC.

serviceAccountFile.description: Filesystem path to the service account JSON key file (used when credentialMode is 'file').

adminEmail.description: Admin email for domain-wide delegation. Required whenever Directory API access is configured.

impersonateServiceAccount.description: GCP service account email to impersonate when using ADC (Workload Identity); must have domain-wide delegation configured.

enableBulkSync.description: Whether Bifrost may bulk-sync users and groups from the Google Workspace Directory API. Set automatically by the SCIM verify step (disabled when the service account is missing the required Directory API scopes); set it explicitly to opt out of bulk sync while keeping login-time claim sync.

product.description: SailPoint product type: 'isc' for Identity Security Cloud, 'iiq' for IdentityIQ

tenant.description: ISC tenant identifier (required for ISC product)

baseUrl.description: IdentityIQ base URL (required for IIQ product)

teamIdsField.description: JWT claim field for team IDs

scim_claim_attributes.description: Per-claim SCIM interpretation. Maps each claim name to its SCIM source type and attribute key.

attributeType.description: 'user' reads from SCIM User resource attributes; 'group' matches SCIM Group resource.

attributeValue.description: SCIM attribute key or group match field for this claim.

scim_provisioning_token.description: Bearer token that inbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning clients (the IdP's SCIM app) must present in the Authorization header to push users and groups to Bifrost. Normally minted in the dashboard (Governance -> User Provisioning) and shown once, but may be seeded here for declarative/GitOps deployments; supports the env. prefix for environment-variable references. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='

scim_auth_proxy.description: Identity-aware proxy (IAP) fronting this SCIM/SSO provider — e.g. Cloudflare Access, a generic OIDC proxy, or AWS ALB (Zero Trust / ZTNA). When enabled, Bifrost takes the login credential from the proxy's header and validates it against the proxy's own keys (not the IdP's), then feeds the resulting claims into the active provider's mapping. Shared across every provider.

enabled.description: Turn the auth-proxy layer on. When false the rest of this block is ignored.

provider.description: Proxy type. 'cloudflare-access' and 'generic' validate OIDC RS256 tokens via JWKS; 'aws-alb' validates ES256 tokens from an AWS ALB via the regional per-kid public key.

mode.description: 'login_only' (default) authenticates an already-provisioned user by identity (email/sub) without deriving permissions from the token. 'full' also runs attribute→role/team/business-unit mapping from the proxy token's claims — the IdP claims used for mapping must be passed through into the proxy-signed token.

headerName.description: Request header carrying the proxy token. Defaults per provider (cloudflare-access: Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion, aws-alb: x-amzn-oidc-data); required for the generic provider. Supports the env. prefix.

issuerUrl.description: Proxy issuer URL, e.g. https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com. Required for the cloudflare-access and generic providers; must be https. Supports the env. prefix.

jwksUrl.description: Explicit JWKS URL for JWKS providers. Derived from issuerUrl for cloudflare-access; empty means OIDC discovery from the issuer (generic). Must be https. Supports the env. prefix.

audience.description: Expected token audience (aud) for JWKS providers, binding the token to this application. Required unless allowedAudiences is set. Supports the env. prefix.

allowedAudiences.description: Alternative to a single audience: a list of accepted audiences. Must not contain blank entries.

region.description: AWS ALB only: region for the public-key endpoint. Derived from the signer ARN when empty. Supports the env. prefix.

expectedSigner.description: AWS ALB only: the ALB ARN to pin the token's signer to. Required for the aws-alb provider — the regional key signs tokens for every ALB in the region, so without this pin any ALB could mint an accepted token. Supports the env. prefix.

publicKeyBaseUrl.description: AWS ALB only: override base URL for the public-key endpoint (keys fetched from <base>/<kid>). Needed for partitions like GovCloud whose endpoint differs from the standard region-derived URL; must be https. Supports the env. prefix.

userIdClaim.description: Token claim used as the user identity. Default 'email'. Supports the env. prefix.

load_balancer_config.description: Adaptive routing settings (Enterprise). Only the keys listed are applied; omitted keys keep their defaults. Settings saved from the dashboard or API are stored in the database and take precedence over this block.

direction_selection_enabled.description: Enable adaptive provider (direction) selection. Defaults to true; omit to leave on.

route_selection_enabled.description: Enable adaptive per-key (route) selection. Defaults to true; omit to leave on.

append_fallbacks_to_pinned.description: When a request already carries a provider, append the healthy providers eligible for its model as fallbacks behind any it configured. Defaults to false.

reroute_failed_directions.description: When a pinned provider is failing for the model, re-route the request to a healthy provider. Defaults to false.

reroute_target.description: Where reroute_failed_directions sends the request: 'pool' picks among the healthy providers adaptive routing scores; 'fallbacks' takes the request's first configured fallback that is not failing, and uses the pool when none is. Defaults to 'pool'.

prune_failed_fallbacks.description: Drop providers that are failing for the model from a request's configured fallbacks. Defaults to false.

history_enabled.description: Record routing history. Defaults to true.

history_retention_days.description: Days of routing history to keep, separate from log retention. Read at startup. Out-of-range values are brought into range. Defaults to 7.

snapshot_persist_interval_seconds.description: How often routing state is saved, in seconds. Out-of-range values are brought into range. Defaults to 300.

guardrails_config.description: Guardrails configuration for content moderation and policy enforcement

description.description: Description of what the rule does

enabled.description: Whether this rule is enabled

target.description: Execution target for the rule. Omitted values default to LLM guardrails.

cel_expression.description: CEL (Common Expression Language) expression for rule evaluation

query.description: Visual rule builder state for the management UI (react-querybuilder). Omitted unless exported from the dashboard. Not evaluated at runtime (cel_expression is).

rules.description: Leaf rules and/or nested combinator+rules groups from the query builder.

apply_to.description: When to apply the guardrail (input, output, or both)

sampling_rate.description: Percentage of requests to apply this rule to (0-100)

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for rule execution

send_all_conversation_turns.description: Whether to send all input conversation turns to the guardrail provider. When false, max_turns_to_send selects the current input plus preceding turns. Omit this field to preserve legacy behavior.

max_turns_to_send.description: Number of preceding conversation turns to include when send_all_conversation_turns is false. 0 sends only the current input.

evaluation_mode.description: How the rule's turns are sent to its guardrail providers. 'bundled' (default) concatenates all turns into one guardrail call. 'per_turn' sends each turn in its own call, evaluated in isolation, to avoid context-sensitive classifiers (e.g. Bedrock prompt-attack) combining unrelated turns into a false-positive block; this scans every turn but uses more provider calls.

stream_replay_event_interval_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between consecutive buffered events after block-capable streaming output guardrails allow the response. 0 sends the buffered events immediately.

output_mode.description: What the rule's output phase does with a match. 'enforce' (default) blocks, redacts, or transforms the response before the client receives it, holding a stream when the rule needs the whole response. 'monitor' delivers the response untouched and never pauses the stream; once the response completes it is evaluated in the background and matches are recorded on the request's log (guardrail_debug detections with enforced: false, redacted stored content, and [output-monitor] plugin logs), never enforced. Monitor requires target 'llm' and apply_to 'output' or 'both'; the input phase of a 'both' rule is always enforced.

provider_config_ids.description: IDs of provider configurations to use with this rule

id.description: Unique identifier for the provider config

access_profiles.description: Enterprise access profile templates for RBAC-driven governance controls

reset_config.description: Window settings the reset duration cannot express. Only valid when reset_duration is quarterly ("1Q").

quarter_start_month.description: First month of Q1 as 1-12, so a fiscal year opening in April (4) gives Apr-Jun / Jul-Sep / Oct-Dec / Jan-Mar. Omitted or 0 means January. Quarter boundaries repeat every three months, so only the value modulo 3 changes the reset dates.

calendar_aligned.description: Deprecated: set calendar_aligned on the parent access profile instead. Kept for backward compatibility with older config.json files; the access-profile reconciler promotes any true value here to the profile's top-level calendar_aligned at load time.

token_max_limit.description: Maximum number of tokens allowed in the reset window

request_max_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed in the reset window

calendar_aligned.description: Deprecated: set calendar_aligned on the parent access profile instead. Kept for backward compatibility with older config.json files; the access-profile reconciler promotes any true value here to the profile's top-level calendar_aligned at load time.

is_active.description: Whether this access profile is active

tags.description: Optional list of tags for filtering and grouping profiles

calendar_aligned.description: Snap budget and rate-limit reset windows to clean calendar boundaries (day, week, month, year) for this profile

allow_all_providers.description: Grant access to every provider, including ones without a provider_configs entry and providers added later. A listed provider keeps its own model allow/blacklist, budgets, rate limits, and key selection; an unlisted provider gets all models, all keys, and no per-provider limits. When false (default), access is deny-by-default via provider_configs.

relay_grants.description: Relays keys governed by this access profile may call, one by one

auto_rotation_interval.description: How often the virtual keys managed by this profile are rotated automatically. Accepts a day count (e.g. "30d") or a Go duration string (e.g. "12h"); integer values are nanoseconds, so prefer strings. 0, an empty string or omitting the field disables scheduled rotation. An enabled schedule must be between 1h and 365d; a profile with an out-of-range value is skipped at startup. Changing the interval re-anchors the next rotation to now + interval.

next_rotation_at.description: Optional RFC 3339 time of the first scheduled rotation; requires an enabled (non-zero) auto_rotation_interval. Defaults to now + interval. Applied when the profile is created or its interval changes; otherwise the stored schedule is kept so a stale export does not rewind it.

provider_configs.description: Per-provider restrictions and limits for this profile

virtual_mcps.description: Virtual MCPs this profile grants. Canonical key; supersedes the deprecated mcp_tool_groups alias, which is ignored when this key is present. An explicit empty array detaches every Virtual MCP from the profile.

mcp_configs.description: Per-MCP-client tool allowlists this profile grants. Canonical key; supersedes the deprecated mcp_servers and mcp_tool_overrides aliases, which are folded into this shape at load time.

mcp_tool_groups.description: DEPRECATED: use virtual_mcps instead. MCP tool group associations, folded into virtual_mcps at load time. Ignored when virtual_mcps is present.

mcp_servers.description: DEPRECATED: use mcp_configs instead. Blanket MCP server grants, folded into mcp_configs at load time as ["*"] allowlists. A client listed in mcp_configs keeps its explicit allowlist; naming one client here and in mcp_configs by different spellings (an id in one, its name in the other) is ambiguous and refused.

mcp_tool_overrides.description: DEPRECATED: use mcp_configs instead. Per-tool include/exclude overrides, folded into mcp_configs allowlists at load time. The new model has no exclude concept, so an exclude only narrows the tools that can be enumerated.

then.$comment: next_rotation_at needs an enabled interval: 0, or a string with no non-zero digit ("", "0", "0s"), disables rotation.

all_models_allowed.description: Whether all models under this provider are allowed

allowed_models.description: Allowed model names (ignored when all_models_allowed is true)

blacklisted_models.description: Models blocked for this provider even if matched by allowed_models (denylist wins). Use ["*"] to block all; empty array or omitted blocks none.

weight.description: Load-balancer seed weight for this provider (null opts out of weighted routing / no override)

model_budgets.description: Per-model budgets and rate limits scoped to this provider. Each entry targets one model and materializes as a user-scoped model config on assignment.

key_ids.description: Key IDs allowed for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all keys; empty array or omitted denies all keys. Specific IDs restrict access to those keys only.

access_profile_provider_model_budget.description: Per-model budget group under an access-profile provider config, with optional per-model rate limit

model_name.description: Model this budget group applies to (scoped to the parent provider)

project.description: A project declared under governance.projects: what it allows, what it may spend, and how that is divided between its members. Members themselves are added from the dashboard or the API.

name.description: Unique project name. Requests reference it with the x-bf-project-name header; the reconciler matches the declaration to the stored project by this name.

is_active.description: Whether the project allows and accounts for anything

expires_at.description: When the project stops allowing anything; omit to never expire

access_rule.description: How the project's own access composes with the access a caller already holds: union leaves the caller's own access untouched (a project with no provider or MCP config then only accounts for spend), intersect permits only what both allow.

membership_mode.description: explicit consults the membership rows; open lets any caller opt in. An open project cannot divide its budget between members.

accounting_mode.description: Which ledgers a request's spend lands on: the project's, the calling principal's, or both

split_policy.description: How the budgets and rate limits the project holds, at every tier (its own, each provider's, and each model's), are divided between members: none leaves them shared, equal gives every member an equal share of each. A change to an equal split's roster or caps recomputes every share in the background.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap the project's budget and rate-limit reset windows to calendar boundaries (day, week, month, quarter, year) instead of rolling from first use. Windows shorter than a day cannot be aligned and stay rolling.

allow_all_providers.description: Grant access to every provider, including ones without a provider_configs entry and providers added later. Listed providers keep their own model, key, budget, and rate-limit rules.

relay_grants.description: Relays requests scoped to this project may call, one by one

disable_content_logging.description: Per-project override of content logging for requests scoped to this project. Omit to inherit what the request's virtual key decides, or client.disable_content_logging when the key has no setting or the request has no key. The project's value overrides the virtual key's in both directions. true keeps request and response content out of the log store and out of observability connector export for the project's traffic. false forces content into the log store even when the virtual key or client setting turns it off, and lifts a virtual key's connector stripping; each connector then follows its own disable_content_logging. The x-bf-disable-content-logging request header, when client.allow_per_request_content_storage_override is on, still takes precedence over this value for the log store.

budgets.description: Project-level spend caps. Declared without ids: on a change, a budget is matched to its stored row by reset_duration so its accumulated spend and window carry over.

provider_configs.description: Per-provider access and accounting, one entry per provider

mcp_configs.description: MCP clients the project allows, one entry per client

virtual_mcps.description: Virtual MCPs assigned to the project, one entry per assignment. A request scoped to the project can reach each one at its /mcp/<slug> endpoint.

project_virtual_mcp.description: A Virtual MCP assigned to a project. Assignments are a set, so a repeat collapses rather than doubling.

virtual_mcp_name.description: Name of the Virtual MCP (as declared under mcp.virtual_mcps) the project is assigned. Resolved to the stored Virtual MCP on startup; a name that matches no Virtual MCP is refused.

virtual_mcp_id.description: Virtual MCP ID, as an alternative to virtual_mcp_name. Wins when both are set. Ids are assigned by the database, so prefer the name in a file that has to be portable across environments.

project_budget.description: A spend cap on a project, a provider inside it, or a model under that provider

reset_duration.description: Reset window, e.g. "1M", "1h", "1Q". Also what pairs a declared budget with its stored row on a change.

reset_config.description: Window settings the reset duration cannot express. Only valid when reset_duration is quarterly ("1Q").

quarter_start_month.description: First month of Q1 as 1-12. Omitted or 0 means January.

project_rate_limit.description: A request and token rate limit on a project, a provider inside it, or a model under that provider. A cap is enforced only with its window, and a limit with neither pair enforces nothing, so at least one complete pair is required.

token_max_limit.description: Maximum number of tokens allowed in the reset window

request_max_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed in the reset window

provider_name.description: Provider name. A project names each provider at most once; on a change the entry is matched to its stored row by this name.

all_models_allowed.description: Whether all models under this provider are allowed

allowed_models.description: Allowed model names (ignored when all_models_allowed is true)

blacklisted_models.description: Models blocked for this provider even if matched by allowed_models (denylist wins). Use ["*"] to block all; empty array or omitted blocks none.

key_ids.description: Key IDs allowed for this provider. Use ["*"] to allow all keys; empty array or omitted allows none, regardless of the top-level version. Specific IDs restrict access to those keys only, and each must belong to this provider.

weight.description: Load-balancer seed weight for this provider (null opts out of weighted routing / no override)

budgets.description: Spend caps on this provider inside the project

model_budgets.description: Per-model budgets and rate limits under this provider, at most one entry per model

project_provider_model_budget.description: Per-model budget group under a project provider config, with optional per-model rate limit

model_name.description: Model this budget group applies to (scoped to the parent provider). The "*" tier is not accepted here; the provider's own budgets cover it.

mcp_client_name.description: Name of the MCP client (as declared under mcp.client_configs) the project allows. Resolved to the stored client on startup; a name that matches no client is refused.

tools_to_execute.description: Tools of the client the project may execute. Use ["*"] to allow every tool; empty array or omitted allows none, regardless of the top-level version.

access_profile_virtual_mcp.description: A Virtual MCP granted to an access profile. Assignments are a set, so a repeat collapses rather than doubling.

virtual_mcp_name.description: Name of the Virtual MCP (as declared under mcp.virtual_mcps) the profile grants. Resolved to the stored Virtual MCP on startup; a name that matches no Virtual MCP is refused.

virtual_mcp_id.description: Virtual MCP ID, as an alternative to virtual_mcp_name. Wins when both are set. Ids are assigned by the database, so prefer the name in a file that has to be portable across environments.

access_profile_mcp_config.description: The tools of one MCP client an access profile may execute.

mcp_client_id.description: MCP client ID or name (names are resolved to client ids at startup)

tools_to_execute.description: Tools the profile may execute. ["*"] means all tools (including future ones); [] means none; a named list means only those tools.

tool_group_id.description: MCP tool group ID (the Virtual MCP's ID; the column kept its old name across the rename)

audit_logs_config.description: Audit logs configuration for CADF-compliant activity logging

disabled.description: Whether audit logging is disabled (default: false)

hmac_key.description: HMAC secret key for signing audit events (minimum 32 bytes). Can use env. prefix for environment variables (e.g., 'env.AUDIT_HMAC_KEY').

retention_days.description: Number of days to retain audit logs (0 means no retention limit)

hmac_keys.description: Named HMAC signing keys for rotation. active_key_id picks the key that signs new events; the others still verify older events. hmac_key, when also set, is the key named "default". Each key needs at least 32 bytes and supports the env. prefix.

id.description: Key ID recorded in each signature, e.g. "2026-q4"

key.description: HMAC secret (minimum 32 bytes). Can use env. prefix (e.g. 'env.AUDIT_HMAC_KEY_2026Q4').

active_key_id.description: ID of the key that signs new audit events. Required when more than one key is configured.

omit_ip_addresses.description: Stop recording client IP addresses in audit logs while keeping every other field. When true, new events are stored without request_ip or initiator host, and IPs from rows written before the setting was enabled are hidden from the API, filter data, search, exports and object storage archives. Existing database rows are not rewritten. Use this where employee privacy rules or works council agreements forbid tracking IPs. Default: false

include_reads.description: Audit every GET request. When false, reads are audited only when they disclose a secret or export data (virtual key reveal/copy, audit log export, downloads) or a handler tags them with an explicit audit action (such as an SSO login) or a high severity. Default: false

archive_interval.description: Archival window size and job period, as a Go duration string (e.g. '24h', '1h', '30m'). Each window is archived as one set of objects. The supported range is 5m and above: this schema accepts any valid duration, and the runtime raises anything shorter to 5m rather than failing startup. Only used when object_storage is set. Default: 24h

archive_grace_period.description: How long to hold a window open past its end before archiving it, as a Go duration string. Absorbs clock skew and late inserts. Must be shorter than archive_interval, otherwise no window would ever close and archival would silently do nothing; the runtime substitutes a safe default if it is not. Only used when object_storage is set. Default: 15m

archive_max_object_bytes.description: Roll a new part object once the current part reaches this many uncompressed bytes. Bounds memory on the archiving node: peak usage is roughly 2x this value when compress is true, since gzip allocates a second full buffer. The minimum and maximum above are strict validation limits — a config outside [1MiB, 4GiB] is rejected as invalid rather than accepted and adjusted. (The runtime additionally clamps to the same range, as a safety net for configs that never pass through schema validation.) Only used when object_storage is set. Default: 134217728 (128MiB)

object_storage.description: Optional object storage for archiving audit events to S3/GCS/Azure Blob. Setting this enables archival; there is no separate on/off flag. A background job periodically copies audit events from the database, one closed time window at a time, writing each window as one or more JSONL part objects plus a manifest listing them: {prefix}/audit-logs/YYYY/MM/DD/{start}-{end}/part-00000.jsonl[.gz] and .../manifest.json[.gz]. Read the manifest to enumerate a window and ignore any object it does not list. The database remains the source of truth and archival never deletes rows (retention_days handles that independently). In a cluster only one node archives a given window. Archival is going-forward only; existing rows are not backfilled. See archive_interval, archive_grace_period and archive_max_object_bytes to tune it.

bucket.description: Bucket name, or Azure Blob container name. Supports env var reference (e.g. env.S3_BUCKET) or a structured secret reference.

prefix.description: Configurable base key path for stored audit objects; the 'audit-logs/' segment is appended under it (default: bifrost)

compress.description: Enable gzip compression for stored objects. Default: false

region.description: AWS region. Supports env var reference

endpoint.description: Custom S3-compatible endpoint for MinIO/R2. Supports env var reference

access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID. Omit to use default credential chain (instance role, env vars, etc.). Supports env var reference

secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key. Supports env var reference

session_token.description: AWS session token for STS temporary credentials. Supports env var reference

role_arn.description: AWS IAM role ARN for STS AssumeRole. Works with static creds or instance role. Supports env var reference

force_path_style.description: Use path-style URLs for S3 (required for MinIO). Default: false

credentials_json.description: GCP service account credentials JSON or file path. Omit to use Application Default Credentials. Supports env var reference

credentials.description: Deprecated: use credentials_json. Kept for backwards compatibility.

project_id.description: GCP project ID override. Supports env var reference

large_payload_optimization.description: Large payload streaming optimization configuration. Detects large request/response payloads and streams them through without full materialization.

enabled.description: Master toggle for large payload optimization (default: false)

request_threshold_bytes.description: Request body size in bytes above which streaming kicks in (default: 10MB)

response_threshold_bytes.description: Response body size in bytes above which streaming kicks in (default: 10MB)

prefetch_size_bytes.description: How much of the request to prefetch for metadata extraction in bytes (default: 64KB)

max_payload_bytes.description: Maximum allowed payload size in bytes; reject above this (default: 500MB)

truncated_log_bytes.description: How many bytes to store as truncated preview in logs (default: 1MB)

websocket_config.description: Optional tuning for the WebSocket gateway (Responses API WebSocket Mode, Realtime API). WebSocket is always enabled; these fields override the high defaults.

max_connections_per_user.description: Maximum concurrent WebSocket connections per user

transcript_buffer_size.description: Number of transcript entries to buffer for Realtime API mid-session fallback

max_idle_per_key.description: Maximum idle connections per provider/key combination

max_total_connections.description: Maximum total idle connections across all providers

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds before an idle connection is evicted

max_connection_lifetime_seconds.description: Maximum lifetime of a connection in seconds

provider_pricing_override.description: Scoped pricing override applied at runtime by the model catalog

virtual_key_id.description: Virtual key ID (required for virtual_key* scopes)

provider_id.description: Provider name (required for provider* scopes; field key remains provider_id for compatibility)

provider_key_name.description: Provider key name alias. Resolved to internal provider key ID at config load time.

match_type.description: How the pattern is matched against model names

pattern.description: Model name pattern to match (exact name or wildcard prefix ending with *)

request_types.description: Request types this override applies to. At least one value is required.

custom_provider_config.description: Custom provider configuration for extending or customizing provider behavior

is_key_less.description: Whether the custom provider requires a key

does_not_send_done_marker.description: Whether the provider ends streams on finish_reason without sending a data: [DONE] marker

wait_for_usage.description: With does_not_send_done_marker, keep reading past finish_reason so the trailing usage-only chunk is collected instead of dropped. Without it the request records zero tokens and zero cost. An upstream that then goes silent ends on network_config.stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds

request_path_overrides.description: Mapping of request type to custom path overriding the default provider path

allowed_requests.description: Allowed request types for the custom provider

responses_retrieve.description: GET stored response by id (OpenAI Responses lifecycle)

responses_cancel.description: POST cancel in-flight stored response (OpenAI Responses lifecycle)

responses_input_items.description: GET list input items for a stored response (OpenAI Responses lifecycle)

circuit_breaker_config.description: Circuit breaker configuration for automatic failover when a provider endpoint degrades

items.description: A single circuit breaker policy that monitors a primary provider+model and redirects to a fallback when the circuit opens

enabled.description: Whether this policy is active. Defaults to false: a policy without enabled: true is stored but inactive.

primary_model.description: Model to monitor as it appears in requests (e.g. 'gpt-4-ptu')

primary_key_ids.description: Optional list of key UUIDs to monitor individually. Each key gets its own sub-circuit; the main circuit opens only when all listed keys are exhausted. Leave empty to use a single shared circuit for all keys serving this provider+model.

fallback_provider.description: Provider to route to when the circuit is open

fallback_model.description: Model to request from the fallback provider when the circuit is open

condition.description: Response signals that trigger the circuit to open

operator.description: OR (default): circuit opens when any signal matches. AND: circuit opens only when all signals match simultaneously. Case-insensitive; empty means OR.

signals.description: List of response signals to evaluate

source.description: What part of the HTTP response to inspect

header_name.description: HTTP response header name to inspect

header_value.description: Trips when the header equals this value (case-insensitive). Mutually exclusive with header_contains.

header_contains.description: Trips when the header value contains this substring (case-insensitive). Mutually exclusive with header_value. If neither is set, trips when the header is present.

default_cooldown.description: How long to keep the circuit open when no header-based cooldown is available. A Go duration string such as '30s', '5m' or '1m30s', or integer nanoseconds. Empty or omitted means 30s.

cooldown_header.description: Response header whose value (in milliseconds) overrides default_cooldown (e.g. 'retry-after-ms'). Falls back to default_cooldown when absent or unparsable.

scim_attribute_role_mappings.description: List of attribute -> role mappings. When a user resolves to more than one role (from these mappings, the native roles claim, or group/attribute channels), roleResolutionStrategy decides which single role is assigned: 'highestPermissionCount' (default) picks the role with the most permissions; 'order' evaluates this mappings list top to bottom and the first matching rule wins.

attribute.description: JWT claim name (supports dot paths, e.g. 'realm_access.roles')

role.description: Bifrost role to assign on match

scim_role_resolution_strategy.description: How a single role is chosen when a user resolves to more than one role: 'highestPermissionCount' (default) picks the role with the most permissions; 'order' evaluates the attribute-role mappings top to bottom and the first matching rule wins.

scim_access_profile_resolution_strategy.description: How many attribute-access-profile grants a user receives when several attributeAccessProfileMappings match: 'all' (default) grants every matching rule's profile; 'order' grants only the profiles of the first rule, in list order, that the user matches. Profiles granted through roles are unaffected.

scim_token_exchange_hosts.description: Hosts besides the issuer's own that an MCP client's token exchange may be sent to through its authorization_server_url (for example an Okta custom authorization server on another domain). The exchange carries the caller's identity-provider token, so only these hosts may be named. Each entry is a bare host name, with a port only when it needs one; entries are lowercased and deduplicated.

scim_cross_app_access.description: Cross App Access (XAA, the ID-JAG profile), inbound: AI clients this identity provider admits for a user exchange a provider-signed ID-JAG at Bifrost's /oauth2/token for a Bifrost token that acts as that user. Needs the governance plugin and client.oauth2_server_config.issuer_url. Client IDs are registered in the dashboard.

enabled.description: Turn Cross App Access on for this provider.

accessTokenTtl.description: Lifetime in seconds of the Bifrost tokens issued for an ID-JAG, 60 to 86400. 0 or omitted uses the default of 86400 (one day), since Okta caps ID-JAGs per user per resource app per month.

provisionUsers.description: Create a Bifrost user for an assertion that names someone who has none, instead of refusing the grant. Off by default: an ID-JAG carries only an ID and email, so most new users would resolve no role.

scim_claims_sync_mode.description: When SCIM is enabled, selects whether IdP login/refresh claims still drive role/team/business-unit/profile sync and JIT user creation: 'both' (default) keeps syncing from both claims and SCIM; 'scim' makes SCIM the sole source of truth — claims are ignored for provisioning and new users must be pushed by SCIM. Inert when SCIM is disabled (claims always sync then).

scim_attribute_team_mappings.description: Attribute -> team mappings (all matches apply). Use value '*' for pass-through.

value.description: Claim value to match, or '*' for pass-through

team.description: Bifrost team slug to assign. In case of '*' value, leave this empty

scim_attribute_access_profile_mappings.description: Attribute -> access-profile mappings. Every matching rule applies: the user is granted the union of the profiles it matches, on top of any profile assigned by role or from the dashboard. Bifrost keeps the tightest limit across the granted profiles.

attribute.description: JWT claim name (supports dot paths, e.g. 'realm_access.roles')

value.description: Claim value to match (case-insensitive). '*' matches whenever the claim carries any non-empty value; glob patterns (e.g. 'bifrost-*') are also supported.

accessProfile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in access_profiles) to grant on match

scim_attribute_project_mappings.description: Attribute -> project mappings. Every matching rule applies: the user is added to each project it matches. Projects are never auto-created; a rule naming a missing project is dropped. Memberships added this way are removed when the rule stops matching; members added from the dashboard are kept.

attribute.description: JWT claim name (supports dot paths, e.g. 'realm_access.roles')

value.description: Claim value to match (case-insensitive). '*' matches whenever the claim carries any non-empty value; glob patterns (e.g. 'bifrost-*') are also supported.

project.description: Name of the project to add the user to on match

scim_bulk_sync_interval.description: How often the directory reconcile lists the IdP's users through its admin API and deprovisions the ones it no longer returns, as whole days or h/m/s pairs (e.g. '12h', '1h30m', '7d'). Must be between 1h and 30d. Defaults to 24h. Inert when SCIM provisioning is enabled or the provider has no directory API access (e.g. Okta without apiToken).

value.description: Claim value to match. Wildcard '*' will use the claim as the name of the business unit to assign.

business_unit.description: Bifrost business unit slug to assign. In case of '*' value, leave this empty

complexity_decision_config.description: Decision-model complexity-classifier request settings. Credentials come from the selected provider's configuration.

provider.description: Provider serving the decision model, e.g. typesafe, or a custom provider with base_provider_type typesafe (Laya, Nimble, Clef). Set together with model; leave both empty for typesafe/jev-latest.

model.description: Decision model to call on the provider, e.g. jev-latest, nimble-latest, english, clef. Set together with provider; leave both empty for typesafe/jev-latest.

previous_message_count.description: Number of preceding user messages sent with the current request. Assistant messages are excluded.

timeout.description: Maximum decision-model classification latency (duration string or milliseconds as a number; default 1500ms).

criteria.description: Per-tier overrides of the shipped decision-model definitions, signals, and examples. Any tier or field left out sends the default.
